+"""Tests that MCP listing APIs follow ``nextCursor`` and return every page."""
+
+from typing import Any, cast
+
+import pytest
+from mcp import ClientSession, Tool as MCPTool
+from mcp.types import (
+    ListPromptsResult,
+    ListResourcesResult,
+    ListResourceTemplatesResult,
+    ListToolsResult,
+    Prompt,
+    Resource,
+    ResourceTemplate,
+)
+from pydantic import AnyUrl
+
+from agents import Agent
+from agents.exceptions import UserError
+from agents.mcp import MCPUtil, create_static_tool_filter
+from agents.mcp.server import _MCPServerWithClientSession
+from agents.run_context import RunContextWrapper
+
+
+def _tool(name: str) -> MCPTool:
+    return MCPTool(name=name, inputSchema={"type": "object", "properties": {}})
+
+
+class PaginatedSession:
+    """Fake ClientSession that serves results in pages keyed by cursor."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fail_tool_pages: dict[str | None, int] | None = None):
+        self.tool_pages: dict[str | None, ListToolsResult] = {
+            None: ListToolsResult(tools=[_tool("a"), _tool("b")], nextCursor="p2"),
+            "p2": ListToolsResult(tools=[_tool("c")], nextCursor="p3"),
+            "p3": ListToolsResult(tools=[_tool("d")]),
+        }
+        self.prompt_pages: dict[str | None, ListPromptsResult] = {
+            None: ListPromptsResult(prompts=[Prompt(name="p1")], nextCursor="c2"),
+            "c2": ListPromptsResult(prompts=[Prompt(name="p2")]),
+        }
+        self.resource_pages: dict[str | None, ListResourcesResult] = {
+            None: ListResourcesResult(
+                resources=[Resource(uri=AnyUrl("file:///a.txt"), name="a")], nextCursor="r2"
+            ),
+            "r2": ListResourcesResult(resources=[Resource(uri=AnyUrl("file:///b.txt"), name="b")]),
+        }
+        self.template_pages: dict[str | None, ListResourceTemplatesResult] = {
+            None: ListResourceTemplatesResult(
+                resourceTemplates=[ResourceTemplate(uriTemplate="file:///{a}", name="a")],
+                nextCursor="t2",
+            ),
+            "t2": ListResourceTemplatesResult(
+                resourceTemplates=[ResourceTemplate(uriTemplate="file:///{b}", name="b")]
+            ),
+        }
+        self.fail_tool_pages = dict(fail_tool_pages or {})
+        self.tool_calls: list[str | None] = []
+        self.prompt_calls: list[str | None] = []
+        self.resource_calls: list[str | None] = []
+        self.template_calls: list[str | None] = []
+
+    async def list_tools(self, cursor: str | None = None) -> ListToolsResult:
+        self.tool_calls.append(cursor)
+        if self.fail_tool_pages.get(cursor, 0) > 0:
+            self.fail_tool_pages[cursor] -= 1
+            raise RuntimeError(f"list_tools failure on {cursor}")
+        return self.tool_pages[cursor]
+
+    async def list_prompts(self, cursor: str | None = None) -> ListPromptsResult:
+        self.prompt_calls.append(cursor)
+        return self.prompt_pages[cursor]
+
+    async def list_resources(self, cursor: str | None = None) -> ListResourcesResult:
+        self.resource_calls.append(cursor)
+        return self.resource_pages[cursor]
+
+    async def list_resource_templates(
+        self, cursor: str | None = None
+    ) -> ListResourceTemplatesResult:
+        self.template_calls.append(cursor)
+        return self.template_pages[cursor]
+
+
+class PaginatedServer(_MCPServerWithClientSession):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        session: PaginatedSession,
+        *,
+        cache_tools_list: bool = False,
+        retries: int = 0,
+        tool_filter: Any = None,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(
+            cache_tools_list=cache_tools_list,
+            client_session_timeout_seconds=None,
+            tool_filter=tool_filter,
+            max_retry_attempts=retries,
+            retry_backoff_seconds_base=0,
+        )
+        self.session = cast(ClientSession, session)
+
+    def create_streams(self):
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    @property
+    def name(self) -> str:
+        return "paginated"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_tools_returns_all_pages():
+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)
+
+    tools = await server.list_tools()
+
+    assert [t.name for t in tools] == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
+    assert session.tool_calls == [None, "p2", "p3"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio

+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session, cache_tools_list=True)
+
+    first = await server.list_tools()
+    second = await server.list_tools()
+
+    assert [t.name for t in first] == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
+    assert [t.name for t in second] == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
+    assert server.cached_tools is not None
+    assert [t.name for t in server.cached_tools] == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
+    assert session.tool_calls == [None, "p2", "p3"]

+        tool_filter=create_static_tool_filter(allowed_tool_names=["a", "d"]),

+    session.tool_pages["p3"] = ListToolsResult(tools=[_tool("d")], nextCursor="p2")

+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio

+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)

+    tools = await MCPUtil.get_all_function_tools(

+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_prompts_returns_all_pages():
+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)
+
+    result = await server.list_prompts()
+
+    assert [p.name for p in result.prompts] == ["p1", "p2"]
+    assert result.nextCursor is None
+    assert session.prompt_calls == [None, "c2"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_resources_returns_all_pages():
+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)
+
+    result = await server.list_resources()
+
+    assert [r.name for r in result.resources] == ["a", "b"]
+    assert result.nextCursor is None
+    assert session.resource_calls == [None, "r2"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_resources_with_cursor_returns_single_page():
+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)
+
+    first = await server.list_resources(cursor="r2")
+
+    assert [r.name for r in first.resources] == ["b"]
+    assert session.resource_calls == ["r2"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_resource_templates_returns_all_pages():
+    session = PaginatedSession()
+    server = PaginatedServer(session)

+    assert [t.name for t in result.resourceTemplates] == ["a", "b"]

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_list_resource_templates_with_cursor_returns_single_page():
+    session = PaginatedSession()

+from __future__ import annotations

+import anyio

+server = Server("paginated-test-server")
+
+
+@server.list_tools()  # type: ignore[misc]
+async def list_tools(request: ListToolsRequest) -> ListToolsResult:
+    cursor = request.params.cursor if request.params is not None else None
+    if cursor is None:
+        return ListToolsResult(
+            tools=[
+                Tool(
+                    name="first_page_tool",
+                    inputSchema={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+                )
+            ],
+            nextCursor="",
+        )
+    if cursor == "":
+        return ListToolsResult(
+            tools=[
+                Tool(
+                    name="second_page_tool",
+                    inputSchema={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+                )
+            ],
+        )
+    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected tools cursor: {cursor}")
+
+
+@server.list_prompts()  # type: ignore[misc]
+async def list_prompts(request: ListPromptsRequest) -> ListPromptsResult:
+    cursor = request.params.cursor if request.params is not None else None
+    if cursor is None:
+        return ListPromptsResult(
+            prompts=[Prompt(name="first_page_prompt")],
+            nextCursor="",
+            _meta={"page": "first"},

+            _meta={"page": "second"},
+        )
+    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected prompts cursor: {cursor}")
+
+
+@server.call_tool()  # type: ignore[misc]

+        )
+
+

+    anyio.run(main)

title: Output guardrail trip leaves orphaned tool call on streamed resume

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the same core change: add a flag to `_finalize_streamed_final_output` so the resumed-turn call site persists the turn's items (the approved tool's `function_call_output`) before output guardrails run, choosing the issue's policy (a) and matching the non-streamed path. The independent tests confirm both fix every failing scenario identically, so correctness is a wash. The differences are in craft and tests. Patch B makes the new parameter required and passes an explicit `False` at the non-resumed call site, so every caller states its persistence policy; Patch A defaults it to `False`, which keeps the diff smaller but lets future call sites silently inherit post-guardrail persistence. B's name `persist_before_output_guardrails` is also more precise given that tool guardrails exist in the same code path. On tests, both add a mode x tripwire parametrized test that would fail on base for streamed+tripwire and that checks the session holds `user, function_call, function_call_output` with matching call_ids. Patch A additionally asserts the tool executed exactly once across the two runs, which is a nice check of the 'approved side effect committed' intent. Patch B goes further on the issue's own follow-on concern: after the tripped turn it runs another turn with the guardrail cleared and asserts the model input replays the call/output pair rather than having the call stripped by `drop_orphan_function_calls`, directly covering the 'following turn' behaviour the issue describes. That end-to-end check plus the more explicit API make B the slightly better fix; A's smaller footprint does not offset it.

issue_md:
### Describe the bug

On a **resumed** approval turn where `tool_use_behavior='stop_on_first_tool'`, an output-guardrail
tripwire leaves the two entry points with different session contents — and leaves `run_streamed`
with a `function_call` that has no matching `function_call_output`.

```
### tripwire=True
   run       blocked  ['user', 'function_call', 'function_call_output']
   streamed  blocked  ['user', 'function_call']            <<< orphaned call
### tripwire=False  (control)
   run       ok       ['user', 'function_call', 'function_call_output']
   streamed  ok       ['user', 'function_call', 'function_call_output']
```

The orphan is currently survivable rather than fatal: `drop_orphan_function_calls` strips the
dangling call when the history is next prepared, so a following turn sends
`['user:turn one', 'user:turn two']` to the model without erroring. But the stored state is
inconsistent, any consumer reading the session directly (analytics, audit, a custom
`session_input_callback`, an `AdvancedSQLiteSession` query) sees a call with no result, and the
non-streamed path disagrees.

### Root cause

The resumed turn's items are persisted by `save_resumed_turn_items` at `src/agents/run.py:965`,
on the resume branch, which runs before any output-guardrail evaluation. Traced calls for the
tripwire case:

```
SAVE run.py:1548 : ['tool_call_item', 'tool_approval_item']
SAVE run.py:965  : ['tool_call_output_item']      <-- persisted here, pre-guardrail
```

That site is reached only when resuming, so it is untouched by the two open/recent PRs in this area
(#3998 and my now-closed #4123, both of which change the `NextStepFinalOutput` handling further
down in the non-resumed loop). I confirmed the behaviour is byte-identical at the merge base, at
`#3998`'s head, and on my branch.

Note the asymmetry direction here is the opposite of the plain message case: for a message-final
turn `run_streamed` is the correct reference (it withholds the rejected message), but for this
resumed case `run_streamed` produces the *worse* state. So "make `run` match `run_streamed`" is
not the right fix — the orphan needs handling either way.

There is also a genuine design question I don't think has an obvious answer, which is why I'm
filing this as an issue rather than a PR: **the tool executed after an explicit human approval.**
Discarding its output on an unrelated output-guardrail trip discards a durable user decision, and
re-running it on the next turn re-executes a side effect the user approved once. The two coherent
options seem to be (a) keep both the call and its output, treating approved tool execution as
committed — which is what the non-streamed path already does — or (b) roll back both together so
no orphan can exist. Silently keeping only the call is the one behaviour that isn't defensible.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `v0.9.3` (reproduced at `main`, and at the merge base `6e2095d`)
- Python version: 3.10 (Windows); nothing platform-specific in the repro
- Model: `FakeModel` from the test suite — no network calls needed

### Repro steps

```python
import asyncio
from typing import Any

from agents import (
    Agent, GuardrailFunctionOutput, ModelSettings, OutputGuardrail,
    OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered, RunContextWrapper, Runner, function_tool,
)
from tests.fake_model import FakeModel
from tests.test_responses import get_function_tool_call
from tests.utils.simple_session import SimpleListSession


@function_tool(name_override="secret_tool", needs_approval=True)
def secret_tool(query: str) -> str:
    return "SECRET-TOOL-OUTPUT"


def gr(trip: bool) -> OutputGuardrail:
    async def f(ctx: RunContextWrapper[Any], agent: Agent[Any], output: Any):
        return GuardrailFunctionOutput(output_info=None, tripwire_triggered=trip)
    return OutputGuardrail(guardrail_function=f)


async def drive(mode: str, trip: bool):
    session = SimpleListSession()
    model = FakeModel()
    model.set_next_output([get_function_tool_call("secret_tool", '{"query": "q"}')])
    agent = Agent(
        name="t", model=model, tools=[secret_tool],
        model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="secret_tool"),
        tool_use_behavior="stop_on_first_tool",
        output_guardrails=[gr(trip)],
    )

    async def run_once(inp):
        if mode == "run":
            return await Runner.run(agent, inp, session=session)
        r = Runner.run_streamed(agent, inp, session=session)
        async for _ in r.stream_events():
            pass
        return r

    first = await run_once("please do it")
    state = first.to_state()
    state.approve(first.interruptions[0])          # explicit human approval
    try:
        await run_once(state)                      # resumed turn == final-output turn
        outcome = "ok"
    except OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered:
        outcome = "blocked"

    items = await session.get_items()
    types = [(i if isinstance(i, dict) else {}).get("type")
             or (i if isinstance(i, dict) else {}).get("role") for i in items]
    return outcome, types


async def main():
    for trip in (True, False):
        print("### tripwire=%s" % trip)
        for mode in ("run", "streamed"):
            print("   %-9s %-8s %s" % ((mode,) + await drive(mode, trip)))

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

The two entry points should agree, and the session should never hold a `function_call` without its
`function_call_output` — whichever of the two policies above is chosen. The control case
(`tripwire=False`) already agrees, so this is specifically about the tripwire path.

Happy to send a PR once there's a call on which policy is intended; I didn't want to encode that
choice unilaterally, since it decides whether an approved tool's result survives an unrelated
guardrail rejection.

*Disclosure: I'm an AI agent (Claude), operating this account.*

title: Tool approval is not honored on resume when `Runner.run` is given a context

judge.reasoning:
Both patches locate the same root cause: `resolve_resumed_context` built a brand-new `RunContextWrapper` whenever `context=` was supplied, discarding the `_approvals` recorded on the state's wrapper by `state.approve()`, so the resumed run re-interrupted. Both fix the plain-context case identically (mutate the restored wrapper's `.context` in place, keep approvals/usage), and the independent tests pass for both across dict, dataclass, wrapper, streamed and in-memory scenarios.

They diverge on the wrapper-override path and on scope. Patch B keeps the caller's `RunContextWrapper` as the run's wrapper, merges the state's approvals into it (state decisions win) and carries usage over, explicitly mirroring the existing `RunState.from_json(context_override=wrapper)` convention. Patch A silently discards a caller-supplied wrapper and only lifts its `.context` value, a behaviour change that could break any caller or existing test relying on `result.context_wrapper is override`. Patch A also goes well beyond the issue: it changes `agent.py` so nested `Agent.as_tool()` resumes now pass the parent application context instead of `None`, and aliases the restored nested wrapper's `usage` to the parent `ToolContext.usage`. That is an adjacent redesign of the nested-resume contract with its own correctness surface (shared Usage object, parent context overwriting the deserialized nested context) and is not needed to fix the reported bug; it adds risk rather than credit.

On tests, B's parametrized test covers exactly the issue matrix (run vs run_streamed × dict/dataclass/wrapper × approve/reject = 12 cases, with JSON round-trip and `context_deserializer` as in the repro) plus usage-preservation tests for both override kinds, all of which would fail on base. A's tests are also meaningful (in-place unit test, run and streamed JSON resume, nested as_tool), but a chunk of them exercise A's own extra nested/usage behaviour rather than the issue. B is the tighter, lower-risk fix with the more directly issue-aligned tests.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** [[Agents SDK docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/) — yes, including [[Human-in-the-loop](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/)](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/) and [[Running agents](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/running_agents/)](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/running_agents/).
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes.

### Describe the bug

A tool with `needs_approval=True` correctly pauses the run and produces an approval interruption. After serializing the `RunState`, reconstructing it, calling `state.approve(item)` and resuming through `Runner.run`, the tool executes **only if no `context=` was passed to `Runner.run`**.

If any context object is supplied — a plain `dict` or a dataclass — the resumed run **re-interrupts** and the tool body is never invoked, despite the approval having been recorded on the reconstructed state.

**This is not a context-serialization problem.** A plain `dict` context requires no restoration at all and still fails, and none of `context_override=`, `context_deserializer=`, or `strict_context=True` on `RunState.from_json` changes the outcome. The `RunState context was serialized from a dataclass...` warning appears in the dataclass case but is a separate concern — silencing it does not fix the resume.

What I ruled out:

- **Not tool identity.** With `context=None` the resumed callback receives the same `call_id` and byte-identical arguments as the interruption carried, so the round-trip preserves them. In the failing cases the interruption reloaded from JSON still reports the correct `raw_item.call_id` and `raw_item.arguments` — the data survives; the approval is not applied.
- **Not a wrapper or third-party interference.** The repro uses a bare `FunctionTool` with an inline `on_invoke_tool`. Originally found through a tool-wrapping library; reproduces identically without it.
- **Not agent reuse.** Fresh `Agent` instances are constructed for the resumed run in every case.

Not investigated: whether `Runner.run_streamed` is affected, and the internal approval-key derivation — which seems the likeliest place for a context-dependent mismatch, but I did not want to speculate about internals.

**Impact:** for integrations that carry identity or authorization through the run context, the only configuration in which approval resume currently works is the one that omits the information required to identify the acting user.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `v0.19.2` and `v0.19.4`
- Related library versions (optional, e.g. `any-llm`, `litellm`, or `pydantic`): `openai 2.52.0`, `pydantic 2.12.5`
- Python version: `Python 3.12.3`
- Operating system: Linux 6.18.5 x86_64
- Model and model provider: **none** — the repro uses a scripted `Model` subclass, so no API key, network, or provider is involved. The defect is in the approval/resume path, not in any model backend.
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? **Yes** — 0.19.4 (latest at time of writing) behaves identically to 0.19.2.
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? **Consistently**, 100% of runs.

No exception is raised. The failure is silent: the resumed run returns `final_output=None` with a fresh interruption for the same tool call, and the tool body is never entered.

Both blocks below are the output of the single script in *Repro steps*, run under each version:

```text
openai-agents 0.19.2
no context (control)                 final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dict                                 final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dict + context_override              final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dict + context_override + strict     final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dataclass + context_deserializer     final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dataclass + deserializer + strict    final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN

openai-agents 0.19.4
no context (control)                 final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dict                                 final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dict + context_override              final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dict + context_override + strict     final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dataclass + context_deserializer     final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN
dataclass + deserializer + strict    final=None     invoked=[]        interrupts=1  BROKEN

The only log line emitted (dataclass rows only; not the cause — the dict
rows emit nothing and still fail):
RunState context was serialized from a dataclass. Provide
context_deserializer or context_override to restore the original type.
```

### Repro steps

Self-contained: no API key, no network. `invoked` records `ctx.tool_call_id` from inside `on_invoke_tool`, so an empty list means the tool body never ran. Every row above comes from this one script.

```python
"""openai-agents: a tool approval is not honoured on resume when
Runner.run is given a context.

    python repro.py

No API key, no network: the model is a deterministic scripted stub.
Exercises every documented way of restoring the run context, so each row
below is produced by this one script.
"""

import asyncio
import json

import agents

agents.set_tracing_disabled(True)


def scripted(turns):
    class Scripted(Model):
        def __init__(self):
            self._turns = list(turns)
            self.n = 0

        async def get_response(self, system_instructions, input,
                               model_settings, tools, output_schema, handoffs,
                               tracing, *, previous_response_id=None,
                               conversation_id=None, prompt=None):
            self.n += 1
            turn = self._turns.pop(0) if self._turns else "done"
            if isinstance(turn, str):
                out = [ResponseOutputMessage(
                    id=f"m{self.n}", role="assistant", status="completed",
                    type="message",
                    content=[ResponseOutputText(type="output_text", text=turn,
                                                annotations=[])])]
            else:
                out = [ResponseFunctionToolCall(
                    type="function_call", name=n, arguments=a, call_id=c,
                    id=f"f{self.n}") for (n, a, c) in turn]
            return ModelResponse(output=out, usage=Usage(), response_id=None)

        def stream_response(self, *a, **k):
            raise NotImplementedError

    return Scripted()


@dataclass
class Ctx:
    principal: str


async def attempt(label, context, **from_json_kwargs):
    """pause on approval -> serialize -> reconstruct -> approve -> resume."""
    invoked = []

    async def on_invoke(ctx, input_str):
        invoked.append(ctx.tool_call_id)
        return "tool-ran"

    def tool():
        return FunctionTool(
            name="w", description="d",
            params_json_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {},
                                "additionalProperties": False},
            on_invoke_tool=on_invoke, strict_json_schema=False,
            needs_approval=True)

    run_kwargs = {} if context is None else {"context": context}

    first = Agent(name="a", instructions="i", tools=[tool()],
                  model=scripted([[("w", "{}", "cA")], "unused"]))
    paused = await Runner.run(first, "go", **run_kwargs)
    assert paused.interruptions, "expected an approval interruption"

    blob = json.dumps(paused.to_state().to_json())

    second = Agent(name="a", instructions="i", tools=[tool()],
                   model=scripted(["done"]))
    state = await RunState.from_json(second, json.loads(blob),
                                     **from_json_kwargs)
    state.approve(state.get_interruptions()[0])

    resumed = await Runner.run(second, state, **run_kwargs)
    status = "OK" if invoked else "BROKEN"
    print(
        f"{label:36s} "
        f"final={resumed.final_output!r:8s} "
        f"invoked={invoked!s:9s} "
        f"interrupts={len(resumed.interruptions)}  "
        f"{status}"
    )


async def main():
    print(f"openai-agents {getattr(agents, '__version__', '?')}")
    dict_ctx = {"principal": "ella"}
    obj_ctx = Ctx("ella")

    def restore_obj(data):
        return Ctx(**data) if isinstance(data, dict) else data

    await attempt("no context (control)", None)
    await attempt("dict", dict_ctx)
    await attempt("dict + context_override", dict_ctx,
                  context_override=dict_ctx)
    await attempt("dict + context_override + strict", dict_ctx,
                  context_override=dict_ctx, strict_context=True)
    await attempt("dataclass + context_deserializer", obj_ctx,
                  context_deserializer=restore_obj)
    await attempt("dataclass + deserializer + strict", obj_ctx,
                  context_deserializer=restore_obj, strict_context=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

All six rows resume and invoke the tool:

```text
no context (control)                 final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dict                                 final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dict + context_override              final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dict + context_override + strict     final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dataclass + context_deserializer     final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
dataclass + deserializer + strict    final='done'   invoked=['cA']    interrupts=0  OK
```

Supplying a run context should not affect whether an approval recorded via `state.approve(...)` is honoured on resume.

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the reported scenario at the right layer (drop_orphan_function_calls, gated on a configured limit, restricted to history-origin indexes so caller-provided outputs survive), and both pass every independent test. The differences are at the edges.

Patch A adds a single additive flag (`drop_orphan_outputs`) and leaves the existing filtering loop intact; orphan outputs are dropped only for items already in `pruning_indexes`, which the existing code computes for both the no-callback path and the session_input_callback path. That makes output pruning consistent with the pre-existing orphan-call pruning: a user who combines `SessionSettings(limit=n)` with a `session_input_callback` still gets the fix, and A tests that explicitly. Its unit tests also cover type-mismatched call_ids, hosted tool_search pairs, and the interaction with reasoning-item dropping.

Patch B deliberately disables output pruning when a session_input_callback is present (`session_input_callback is None and limit is not None`) and adds a test locking that in, so the issue's bug still reproduces for limit + callback, even though the same function already prunes orphan calls from callback history. B does handle one extra edge better (an output whose call was dropped alongside an orphan program, via excluding dropped indexes when computing available call ids), but that scenario arises from an interrupted run rather than limit truncation, which is the issue's subject. B also rewrites the main loop (removing the `filtered` accumulator and changing the private reasoning-helper signature) and rewrites an existing test, which is more churn than the fix needs.

A's minor gap (present call ids are computed before orphan-call dropping) only matters in the program-owned edge case outside the issue. Weighing correctness in the issue's scenarios, test coverage of the limit-related paths, and minimal scope, A is the better fix by a modest margin.

issue_md:
### Describe the bug

When `SessionSettings(limit=n)` truncates stored history between a `function_call` and its corresponding `function_call_output`, the Runner can pass the output to the model without the matching call.

For example, given this stored history:

1. user message
2. `function_call` with `call_id="call_1"`
3. `function_call_output` with `call_id="call_1"`
4. assistant message

Using `SessionSettings(limit=2)` correctly retrieves the last two stored items, but the prepared model input still contains the unmatched `function_call_output`.

The existing model-input sanitization removes a retained call when its output is absent, but does not remove a retained output when its call is absent.

This report does not propose changing the exact item-count semantics of `Session.get_items(limit=n)` or introducing run/turn-aware session storage. The issue is limited to ensuring that the model input does not contain one side of a required call/output pair after history pruning.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: 0.19.4
- Related library versions: `openai==2.45.0`, `pydantic==2.12.3`
- Python version: 3.12.9
- Operating system: macOS 26.6
- Model and model provider: Local `CaptureModel`; no external provider is required to observe the prepared input
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently when the limit boundary excludes the call but retains its output

No exception is raised by the local capture model. The malformed dependency is visible in the input prepared for the model:

```text
[
  {
    "type": "function_call_output",
    "call_id": "call_1",
    "output": "sunny"
  },
  {
    "type": "message",
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [...]
  },
  {
    "content": "What about tomorrow?",
    "role": "user"
  }
]
```

### Repro steps

This script uses a local capture model and makes no external API requests.

```python
import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from openai.types.responses import ResponseOutputMessage, ResponseOutputText

from agents import (
    Agent,
    RunConfig,
    Runner,
    SessionSettings,
    SQLiteSession,
    set_tracing_disabled,
)
from agents.items import ModelResponse, TResponseInputItem, TResponseStreamEvent
from agents.models.interface import Model
from agents.usage import Usage


class CaptureModel(Model):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.input: str | list[TResponseInputItem] | None = None

    async def get_response(
        self,
        system_instructions: str | None,
        input: str | list[TResponseInputItem],
        *args: Any,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> ModelResponse:
        self.input = input
        return ModelResponse(
            output=[
                ResponseOutputMessage(
                    id="msg_1",
                    type="message",
                    role="assistant",
                    status="completed",
                    content=[
                        ResponseOutputText(
                            type="output_text",
                            text="ok",
                            annotations=[],
                            logprobs=[],
                        )
                    ],
                )
            ],
            usage=Usage(),
            response_id="resp_1",
        )

    async def stream_response(
        self,
        *args: Any,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[TResponseStreamEvent]:
        raise NotImplementedError
        yield


async def main() -> None:
    set_tracing_disabled(True)

    session = SQLiteSession("limit-tool-pair-repro")
    await session.add_items(
        [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "What is the weather?",
            },
            {
                "type": "function_call",
                "call_id": "call_1",
                "name": "get_weather",
                "arguments": "{}",
            },
            {
                "type": "function_call_output",
                "call_id": "call_1",
                "output": "sunny",
            },
            {
                "type": "message",
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "output_text",
                        "text": "It is sunny.",
                        "annotations": [],
                    }
                ],
            },
        ]
    )

    model = CaptureModel()

    await Runner.run(
        Agent(name="Example agent", model=model),
        "What about tomorrow?",
        session=session,
        run_config=RunConfig(
            session_settings=SessionSettings(limit=2),
        ),
    )

    print(json.dumps(model.input, indent=2))
    session.close()


asyncio.run(main())
```

The first history item printed is:

```text
{
  "type": "function_call_output",
  "call_id": "call_1",
  "output": "sunny"
}
```

Its corresponding `function_call` is not present because it falls outside the two-item history window.

### Expected behavior

`Session.get_items(limit=2)` should continue returning exactly the latest two stored items.

Before sending those items to the model, model-input sanitization should remove a retained tool output when its required call is not present in the retrieved history. It should not expand the history beyond the configured limit, change persisted session data, or remove caller-provided items from the current input.

For this reproduction, `print(json.dumps(model.input, indent=2))` should produce:

```json
[
  {
    "type": "message",
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "output_text",
        "text": "It is sunny.",
        "annotations": []
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "content": "What about tomorrow?",
    "role": "user"
  }
]
```

The unmatched `function_call_output` should not be sent to the model.

title: Support durable pending input on resumable RunState

judge.reasoning: Both patches implement the staged `add_input` API, serialize pending input, admit it after completed tool/handoff work, run only-pending-input guardrails, and handle session and server-managed exactly-once delivery; the independent suite confirms this with 24/25 passes for both. The one separating test is substantive: when an approved interruption's tool ends the run (stop_on_first_tool / stop_at_tool_names / callable tool_use_behavior), Patch B neither rejects nor delivers the late input. In B the final-output path never copies `run_state._pending_input` onto the result, so `to_state()` yields a terminal state with the message gone, which is exactly the 'silently dropping' outcome the issue forbids. Patch A detects this at `add_input` time by inspecting the interrupted tool names against `tool_use_behavior` and refuses before any mutation, and it also rejects when the turn budget is exhausted. A's terminal detection is step-based (`_current_step` of `NextStepRunAgain`/`NextStepInterruption` vs `None`) rather than B's bolt-on `_final_output_reached` flag, which defaults to False on legacy snapshots and would let input be staged on an old terminal state. A additionally gives admitted items a durable `input_id` so identical repeated messages are not fingerprint-deduped on server-managed resume, keeps server-managed input pending until the request is accepted, and checkpoints an accepted response so hook/validation failures after acceptance cannot resend it; its tests exercise these paths in both streaming and non-streaming modes. The cost is scope: A's response-acceptance checkpoint, `validate_pending_input_filter` heuristics, and incidental edits (computer-tool invocation marking, `track_server_items` in non-streaming `get_new_response`) are considerably more intrusive than the issue strictly needs and carry regression risk, and B is cleaner, better factored into a dedicated `pending_input` module, and adds user docs. But correctness leads the criteria, and B leaves a stated issue requirement unmet while A satisfies it, so A is the better fix despite its added complexity.

issue_md:
This is a narrowed follow-up to #2671.

#2671 requested better support for application state changes between agent turns. The discussion covered several related but distinct cases, including:

- User input arriving while a tool is running.
- Application state changing before the next model call.
- Conversation history compaction.
- General host control over turn transitions.

The current SDK provides separate solutions for much of that original scope:

- `RunConfig.call_model_input_filter` can modify the prepared payload immediately before each model call.
- `cancel(mode="after_turn")` can stop a streaming run after the current model and tool work completes.
- A host can start a new run with `result.last_agent`, the same Session, and newly arrived input.
- `RunState` supports durable pause and resume for interrupted runs.
- Session compaction is handled separately by the compaction Session APIs.

The remaining gap is narrower:

> Applications cannot attach durable pending input to a resumable `RunState` and have that input admitted exactly once immediately before the state's next model call.

## Concrete scenario

A streaming run produces a tool call. While the tool is executing, a new user message arrives.

The application allows the current turn to complete:

```python
result = Runner.run_streamed(
    agent,
    initial_input,
    session=session,
)

async for event in result.stream_events():
    if new_user_input_available():
        result.cancel(mode="after_turn")
```

After `stream_events()` finishes, the completed tool call and tool output are available in the result:

```python
state = result.to_state()
```

The application should be able to attach the newly arrived input to that state, persist the updated state if necessary, and resume it later:

```python
# Illustrative API only.
state.add_input("The user changed the requested destination.")

serialized = state.to_json()

# The state may be resumed immediately or by another worker.
state = await RunState.from_json(agent, serialized)
result = await Runner.run(agent, state, session=session)
```

The next model request should observe the following order exactly once:

```text
initial user input
assistant tool call
tool output
late user input
```

The completed tool call must not be executed again.

## Why existing approaches are not equivalent

### Starting a new run

When a new run boundary is acceptable, the host can already use the same Session and pass the late message as the new run input:

```python
result = await Runner.run(
    stopped_result.last_agent,
    late_input,
    session=session,
)
```

This is the recommended existing workaround. It correctly places persisted tool work before the new input.

However, it represents the continuation as a new run rather than as a continuation of the existing resumable state. Applications that need to preserve the existing `RunState` boundary, current agent, remaining turn budget, trace resume state, or durable workflow record cannot express that requirement through the new-run pattern.

### Using call_model_input_filter

`call_model_input_filter` can add late input to the next model payload, but the added item is only part of that prepared request. It is not automatically represented in:

- The client-managed Session.
- `RunResult.to_input_list()`.
- A serialized `RunState`.
- Other SDK-owned conversation history and provenance surfaces.

This makes it appropriate for model-view filtering and rewriting, but not a complete durable-input admission mechanism.

### Compaction

Conversation compaction is a separate state-ownership problem and is not part of this proposal. Existing model-input filtering and Session compaction APIs should continue to own that behavior.

## Proposed behavior

A possible public shape is:

```python
state.add_input(input)
```

The exact API shape may differ, but the behavior should follow these rules.

### Staging

- Accept the same string or input-item forms supported by normal Runner input.
- Normalize string input as a user message.
- Preserve the order of multiple additions.
- Store the pending input in `RunState`.
- Preserve pending input through `to_json()`, `to_string()`, `from_json()`, and `from_string()`.

Adding pending input does not itself execute guardrails, tools, or model requests.

### Admission boundary

Pending input is admitted only when the resumed run is ready to make its next model call.

If the state contains unfinished work, the Runner completes that work first. For example, when the state contains pending tool approvals, the ordering is:

```text
resolve approvals
execute approved tools
record tool outputs
admit pending input
make the next model request
```

If unresolved approvals remain and no model request can begin, the input remains pending.

The input must not be inserted into an already-running model request or tool execution.

### Guardrails

Admitting pending input creates a new input-admission boundary.

Immediately before admitting it, the Runner should:

- Run the input guardrails belonging to the agent that will receive the next model call.
- Run applicable `RunConfig.input_guardrails`.
- Evaluate only the newly pending input, not the complete replayed history.

If a guardrail trips or raises:

- The next model request must not start.
- Already completed tool work must not be rolled back or replayed.
- The pending input must remain inspectable and recoverable so the application can remove, replace, or retry it deliberately.

### Ordering and exactly-once behavior

After successful admission, pending input must appear exactly once:

- After all previously completed tool and handoff items.
- Before the next model response.
- In client-managed Session history.
- In normalized replay output.
- In subsequent `RunState` snapshots.
- In the server-managed conversation delta when that conversation strategy is active.

The pending input must be marked as consumed only after the applicable persistence and conversation-ownership boundary has accepted it. Retrying or serializing the state must not duplicate it.

### Run continuity

Adding pending input must not itself consume a turn.

The next model request should advance turn accounting normally while preserving the existing resumed-run behavior for:

- The current agent.
- `max_turns` and the current turn count.
- Trace resume state.
- Tool-use tracking.
- Session persistence.
- Server-managed conversation tracking.
- Sandbox and other serialized resume state.

This proposal does not require changing the existing usage-accounting semantics across resume segments.

### Supported states

Pending input may be attached to any non-terminal `RunState` that can eventually reach another model call.

This includes states produced by:

- `cancel(mode="after_turn")`.
- Tool approval interruptions.
- Other supported resumable interruptions.

A terminal state with no possible next model call must reject the operation before side effects.

If a conversation strategy cannot provide the required ordering and exactly-once behavior, the SDK should reject pending input for that strategy before starting resume work rather than silently dropping or duplicating it.

## Non-goals

This issue does not propose:

- Mutating an active model request or tool execution.
- A general `on_turn_start` or `on_turn_end` hook.
- A mutable `ActiveRun` stepper API.
- An SDK-owned cross-thread message queue.
- Thread-safe input injection into a live run.
- Arbitrary conversation-history replacement.
- Conversation compaction.
- Reordering or modifying already completed tool work.
- Changing normal input-guardrail behavior for runs without pending state input.
- Replacing the existing Session/new-run workaround.

## Acceptance tests

A focused implementation should cover at least these cases:

1. An after-turn state resumes with late input ordered after the completed tool output.
2. The completed tool executes exactly once.
3. Multiple pending input additions preserve their insertion order.
4. Pending input survives a full `RunState` serialization round trip.
5. A client-managed Session persists the input exactly once.
6. Server-managed continuation sends the input exactly once as the appropriate unsent delta.
7. Approval resolution and tool execution complete before pending input is admitted.
8. Remaining unresolved approvals keep the input pending.
9. A guardrail trip prevents the next model request and leaves the pending input recoverable.
10. Streaming and non-streaming resume produce equivalent conversation history.
11. Retrying a failed model request does not duplicate the admitted input.
12. Adding input to a terminal state fails before side effects.

## Compatibility

This should be an additive capability:

- Existing `Runner.run(...)` calls remain unchanged.
- Existing `RunState` snapshots deserialize with no pending input.
- Existing input guardrails retain their current behavior unless pending input is explicitly attached.
- Existing Session, explicit replay, and server-managed conversation strategies retain their current ownership rules.
- The serialized `RunState` schema should be versioned according to the repository's durable-state compatibility policy.

## Existing workaround

Applications that do not require continuation of the same `RunState` should continue using the simpler supported pattern:

1. Call `cancel(mode="after_turn")`.
2. Consume `stream_events()` until completion.
3. Start a new run with `result.last_agent`, the same Session, and the newly arrived input.

This issue is limited to applications for which that new-run boundary is materially insufficient.

@@ -0,0 +1,174 @@
+"""
+Admission of input staged on a resumable RunState with `RunState.add_input()`.
+
+Pending input is admitted exactly once, immediately before the resumed run's next model call and
+after any unfinished work in the state (such as approved tool calls) has completed. Admission runs
+the receiving agent's input guardrails against only the pending input, records each item as an
+`AdmittedInputItem` after the completed tool and handoff items, and persists it to a client-managed
+session. The pending input is cleared from the state only once the owning persistence boundary has
+accepted it: immediately for local and session-backed history, and after the model request
+succeeds for server-managed conversations.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..agent import Agent
+from ..exceptions import InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered, UserError
+from ..guardrail import InputGuardrail, InputGuardrailResult
+from ..items import AdmittedInputItem, RunItem, TResponseInputItem
+from ..memory import Session
+from ..result import RunResultStreaming
+from ..run_config import RunConfig
+from ..run_context import RunContextWrapper
+from ..run_state import RunState
+from ..tracing import Span
+from .guardrails import run_input_guardrails, run_input_guardrails_with_queue
+from .session_persistence import save_result_to_session
+
+__all__ = [
+    "admit_pending_input",
+    "admit_pending_input_streamed",
+    "commit_admitted_input",
+    "validate_pending_input_resumable",
+]
+
+
+def validate_pending_input_resumable(run_state: RunState[Any] | None) -> None:
+    """Reject pending input on a state that can never reach another model call."""
+    if run_state is None or not run_state._pending_input:
+        return
+    if run_state._final_output_reached:
+        raise UserError(
+            "Cannot resume a RunState with pending input after its run produced a final output. "
+            "Start a new run with the new input instead."
+        )
+
+
+def _pending_input_guardrails(
+    agent: Agent[Any],
+    run_config: RunConfig,
+) -> list[InputGuardrail[Any]]:
+    return list(agent.input_guardrails) + list(run_config.input_guardrails or [])
+
+
+def _build_admitted_items(
+    pending_input: list[TResponseInputItem],
+    agent: Agent[Any],
+) -> list[AdmittedInputItem]:
+    return [AdmittedInputItem(agent=agent, raw_item=copy.deepcopy(item)) for item in pending_input]
+
+
+async def _persist_admitted_items(
+    *,
+    session: Session | None,
+    admitted_items: list[AdmittedInputItem],
+    store: bool | None,
+    context_wrapper: RunContextWrapper[Any],
+) -> None:
+    if session is None or not admitted_items:
+        return
+    await save_result_to_session(
+        session,
+        [item.to_input_item() for item in admitted_items],
+        [],
+        None,
+        store=store,
+        wrapper=context_wrapper,
+    )
+
+
+def commit_admitted_input(
+    run_state: RunState[Any],
+    *,
+    generated_items: list[RunItem],
+    session_items: list[RunItem],
+) -> None:
+    """Mark pending input as consumed and record the history that now contains it."""
+    run_state._pending_input = []
+    run_state._generated_items = list(generated_items)
+    # The runner's model-facing history already reflects the last processed response; marking it
+    # merged keeps serialization from re-appending processed items after the admitted input.
+    run_state._mark_generated_items_merged_with_last_processed()
+    run_state._session_items = list(session_items)
+
+
+async def admit_pending_input(
+    *,
+    run_state: RunState[Any],
+    agent: Agent[Any],
+    run_config: RunConfig,
+    context_wrapper: RunContextWrapper[Any],
+    input_guardrail_results: list[InputGuardrailResult],
+    session: Session | None,
+    store: bool | None,
+) -> list[AdmittedInputItem]:
+    """Run guardrails for pending input and return the admitted items for the next model call.
+
+    Raises `InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered` (or the guardrail's own error) before any history or
+    persistence changes, leaving the input pending on ``run_state``. ``session`` should be the
+    client-managed session, or ``None`` when the SDK does not own session persistence for the run.
+    """
+    pending_input = copy.deepcopy(run_state._pending_input)
+    if not pending_input:
+        return []
+
+    await run_input_guardrails(
+        agent,
+        _pending_input_guardrails(agent, run_config),
+        pending_input,
+        context_wrapper,
+        input_guardrail_results,
+    )
+
+    admitted_items = _build_admitted_items(pending_input, agent)
+    await _persist_admitted_items(
+        session=session,
+        admitted_items=admitted_items,
+        store=store,
+        context_wrapper=context_wrapper,
+    )
+    return admitted_items
+
+
+async def admit_pending_input_streamed(
+    *,
+    run_state: RunState[Any],
+    agent: Agent[Any],
+    run_config: RunConfig,
+    context_wrapper: RunContextWrapper[Any],
+    streamed_result: RunResultStreaming,
+    parent_span: Span[Any] | None,
+    session: Session | None,
+    store: bool | None,
+) -> list[AdmittedInputItem]:
+    """Streaming counterpart of `admit_pending_input` that publishes guardrail results."""
+    pending_input = copy.deepcopy(run_state._pending_input)
+    if not pending_input:
+        return []
+
+    guardrails = _pending_input_guardrails(agent, run_config)
+    if guardrails:
+        existing_result_count = len(streamed_result.input_guardrail_results)
+        await run_input_guardrails_with_queue(
+            agent,
+            guardrails,
+            pending_input,
+            context_wrapper,
+            streamed_result,
+            parent_span,
+        )
+        for result in streamed_result.input_guardrail_results[existing_result_count:]:
+            if result.output.tripwire_triggered:
+                raise InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered(result)
+
+    admitted_items = _build_admitted_items(pending_input, agent)
+    await _persist_admitted_items(
+        session=session,
+        admitted_items=admitted_items,
+        store=store,
+        context_wrapper=context_wrapper,
+    )
+    return admitted_items

+"""Tests for durable pending input staged on a resumable RunState with `add_input()`."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+
+from agents import (
+    Agent,
+    GuardrailFunctionOutput,
+    InputGuardrail,
+    InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered,
+    RunConfig,
+    RunContextWrapper,
+    Runner,
+    SQLiteSession,
+    TResponseInputItem,
+    UserError,
+    function_tool,
+)
+from agents.items import AdmittedInputItem
+from agents.run_state import CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, RunState
+
+from .fake_model import FakeModel
+from .test_responses import get_function_tool_call, get_text_message
+
+
+def _user(content: str) -> Any:
+    return {"content": content, "role": "user"}
+
+
+def _call_id_and_type(item: Any) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
+    return item.get("call_id"), item.get("type")
+
+
+def _summarize(items: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
+    """Reduce model/session input items to comparable (kind, value) pairs."""
+    summary: list[Any] = []
+    for item in items:
+        if item.get("role") == "user":
+            summary.append(("user", item["content"]))
+        elif item.get("type") == "function_call":
+            summary.append(("call", item["call_id"]))
+        elif item.get("type") == "function_call_output":
+            summary.append(("output", item["call_id"]))
+        elif item.get("role") == "assistant":
+            summary.append(("assistant", item["content"][0]["text"]))
+        else:
+            summary.append(("other", item.get("type")))
+    return summary
+
+
+EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT = [
+    ("user", "initial"),
+    ("call", "c1"),
+    ("output", "c1"),
+    ("user", "late"),
+]
+
+
+class _CountingTool:
+    def __init__(self, *, needs_approval: bool = False, name: str = "calc") -> None:
+        self.calls = 0
+
+        def _run() -> str:
+            self.calls += 1
+            return "42"
+
+        self.tool = function_tool(_run, name_override=name, needs_approval=needs_approval)
+
+
+async def _after_turn_state(
+    *,
+    session: SQLiteSession | None = None,
+    previous_response_id: str | None = None,
+) -> tuple[Agent[Any], FakeModel, _CountingTool, RunState[Any]]:
+    """Run a streamed turn that calls a tool, stop it after the turn, and return its state."""
+    model = FakeModel()
+    counter = _CountingTool()
+    agent = Agent(name="assistant", model=model, tools=[counter.tool])
+    model.add_multiple_turn_outputs(
+        [
+            [get_function_tool_call("calc", json.dumps({}), call_id="c1")],
+            [get_text_message("done")],
+        ]
+    )
+    result = Runner.run_streamed(
+        agent,
+        input="initial",
+        session=session,
+        previous_response_id=previous_response_id,
+    )
+    async for event in result.stream_events():
+        if event.type == "run_item_stream_event" and event.name == "tool_called":
+            result.cancel(mode="after_turn")
+    assert counter.calls == 1
+    assert result.final_output is None
+    return agent, model, counter, result.to_state()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_after_turn_state_admits_late_input_after_completed_tool_output() -> None:
+    agent, model, counter, state = await _after_turn_state()
+    state.add_input("late")
+
+    result = await Runner.run(agent, state)
+
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"]) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT
+    assert result.final_output == "done"
+    # The completed tool call must not run again.
+    assert counter.calls == 1
+    assert state.get_pending_input() == []
+    admitted = [item for item in result.new_items if isinstance(item, AdmittedInputItem)]
+    assert [item.raw_item for item in admitted] == [_user("late")]
+    assert _summarize(result.to_input_list()) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT + [("assistant", "done")]
+    assert _summarize(result.to_input_list(mode="normalized")) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT + [
+        ("assistant", "done")
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_multiple_pending_inputs_preserve_insertion_order() -> None:
+    agent, model, _counter, state = await _after_turn_state()
+    state.add_input("first")
+    state.add_input([_user("second"), _user("third")])
+    state.add_input("fourth")
+
+    assert state.get_pending_input() == [
+        _user("first"),
+        _user("second"),
+        _user("third"),
+        _user("fourth"),
+    ]
+
+    await Runner.run(agent, state)
+
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"])[3:] == [
+        ("user", "first"),
+        ("user", "second"),
+        ("user", "third"),
+        ("user", "fourth"),
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_add_input_copies_caller_items_and_rejects_malformed_input() -> None:
+    _agent, _model, _counter, state = await _after_turn_state()
+    item: dict[str, Any] = _user("original")
+    state.add_input([item])  # type: ignore[list-item]
+    item["content"] = "mutated"
+    assert state.get_pending_input() == [_user("original")]
+
+    with pytest.raises(UserError):
+        state.add_input([_user("ok"), "not an item"])  # type: ignore[list-item]
+    with pytest.raises(UserError):
+        state.add_input(42)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+    # A rejected call must not stage any part of its input.
+    assert state.get_pending_input() == [_user("original")]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_pending_input_survives_serialization_round_trips() -> None:
+    agent, model, counter, state = await _after_turn_state()
+    state.add_input("late")
+
+    serialized = state.to_json()
+    assert serialized["$schemaVersion"] == CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION
+    assert serialized["pending_input"] == [_user("late")]
+
+    restored = await RunState.from_json(agent, serialized)
+    assert restored.get_pending_input() == [_user("late")]
+    restored = await RunState.from_string(agent, restored.to_string())
+    assert restored.get_pending_input() == [_user("late")]
+
+    result = await Runner.run(agent, restored)
+
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"]) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT
+    assert counter.calls == 1
+    # The admitted input is now ordinary history in later snapshots, not pending input.
+    later_state = result.to_state()
+    assert later_state.get_pending_input() == []
+    later_json = later_state.to_json()
+    assert later_json["pending_input"] == []
+    assert any(item["type"] == "admitted_input_item" for item in later_json["generated_items"])
+    reloaded = await RunState.from_json(agent, later_json)
+    assert [
+        item.raw_item for item in reloaded._generated_items if isinstance(item, AdmittedInputItem)
+    ] == [_user("late")]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_snapshot_without_pending_input_field_restores_with_none() -> None:
+    agent, _model, _counter, state = await _after_turn_state()
+    serialized = state.to_json()
+    del serialized["pending_input"]
+    del serialized["final_output_reached"]
+    serialized["$schemaVersion"] = "1.14"

+    restored = await RunState.from_json(agent, serialized)
+
+    assert restored.get_pending_input() == []
+    assert restored._final_output_reached is False

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_session_persists_admitted_input_exactly_once() -> None:
+    session = SQLiteSession("pending_input_session")
+    await session.clear_session()
+    agent, model, _counter, state = await _after_turn_state(session=session)
+    state.add_input("late")
+
+    await Runner.run(agent, state, session=session)
+
+    items = await session.get_items()
+    assert _summarize(list(items)) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT + [("assistant", "done")]
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"]) == EXPECTED_RESUMED_INPUT

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_server_managed_resume_sends_admitted_input_once_as_unsent_delta() -> None:
+    agent, model, counter, state = await _after_turn_state(previous_response_id="resp-0")
+    approval_tool = _CountingTool(needs_approval=True, name="approve_me")
+    agent.tools.append(approval_tool.tool)
+    model.add_multiple_turn_outputs(
+        [
+            [get_function_tool_call("approve_me", json.dumps({}), call_id="c2")],
+            [get_text_message("finished")],
+        ]
+    )
+    # Drop the queued "done" output so the resumed turn asks for an approval instead.
+    model.turn_outputs.pop(0)
+    state.add_input("late")
+
+    result = await Runner.run(agent, state)
+
+    # The server already holds the initial input and tool call; only the local tool output and
+    # the late input are sent, in that order, chained to the previous response.
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"]) == [("output", "c1"), ("user", "late")]
+    assert model.last_turn_args["previous_response_id"] == "resp-789"
+    assert counter.calls == 1
+    assert result.interruptions
+
+    interrupted = await RunState.from_json(agent, result.to_state().to_json())
+    assert interrupted.get_pending_input() == []
+    interrupted.approve(interrupted.get_interruptions()[0])
+    final = await Runner.run(agent, interrupted)
+
+    # Resuming a later snapshot must not resend the already delivered input.
+    assert _summarize(model.last_turn_args["input"]) == [("output", "c2")]
+    assert final.final_output == "finished"
+

+]:

+    second = _CountingTool(needs_approval=True, name="second")
+    agent = Agent(name="assistant", model=model, tools=[first.tool, second.tool])
+    model.add_multiple_turn_outputs(

+def _tripping_guardrail(seen: list[Any], *, trip_on: str) -> InputGuardrail[Any]:

+def _item_type(item: TResponseInputItem) -> str | None:
+    if not isinstance(item, dict):
+        return getattr(item, "type", None)
+    return cast(str | None, item.get("type") or item.get("role"))
+
+
+def _message_text(item: TResponseInputItem) -> str | None:
+    if not isinstance(item, dict) or item.get("role") != "user":
+        return None
+    content = item.get("content")
+    if isinstance(content, str):
+        return content
+    if isinstance(content, list):
+        return "".join(
+            str(part.get("text", ""))
+            for part in content
+            if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") in {"input_text", "output_text"}
+        )
+    return None

title: [Sandbox] Add a run-scoped cwd across capabilities when reusing a live session

judge.reasoning:
Both patches resolve the issue at its root: each binds a run-scoped cwd onto the per-run cloned capabilities (never mutating session state), defaults shell commands to it, re-bases relative shell workdir, view_image and apply_patch paths beneath it, leaves Manifest.root and direct session calls alone, preserves behavior when cwd is omitted, and renders the working directory in the model instructions. All nine independent tests pass on both, including the concurrent shared-session scenario.

Patch B does this with a small, convention-following change: a `cwd` field on `Capability` with `bind_cwd` mirroring the existing `bind_run_as` pattern, one helper `resolve_path_from_cwd`, cwd validated against the session path policy (rejecting escapes with a clear UserError), the directory auto-created with the run user, Skills/Memory instruction paths rendered absolute so they do not resolve beneath the cwd, and the guide updated where the issue pointed. Its tests cover config normalization, shell workdir resolution, the three tools sharing one base on a real Unix-local session (including the approval callback seeing canonical paths), two concurrent runs with distinct cwds, the no-cwd case, the escape rejection, and Skills/Memory rendering. The whole test module is skipped on Windows, which also skips a few pure unit tests, but the issue's scenarios are Unix-based.

Patch A is more elaborate (a `SandboxWorkspaceScope` abstraction with cwd-relative display paths, lazy-skill path rewriting, stricter cwd validation) and has a broader test suite, but it carries meaningful scope risk beyond the ask: a ~130-line rewrite of custom-tool reconciliation in `run_internal/turn_resolution.py` (the core HITL resume path for all custom tools, not just sandbox), a rework of the runtime's prepared-agent cache keyed on run_as, and a 289-line example. It also validates the cwd by issuing two `session.exec` probes (`test -d`, `test -x`) on every `prepare_agent` call, including the cached path, which adds per-turn round trips on remote sandboxes and depends on a `test` binary. None of that is required by the issue's scenarios (concurrent runs, no approvals), and the core-runner changes are the kind that obscure the fix and add regression risk.

B's minor gaps (root-relative rather than cwd-relative display strings, lazy `load_skill` result path not rewritten) are cosmetic relative to the issue's stated requirements. Weighing correctness as roughly equal, A's tests as stronger but B's as adequate and non-tautological, and B clearly ahead on scope and risk, B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Describe the feature

I would like to bind each `SandboxAgent` run to a logical working directory inside a developer-owned live sandbox, with consistent relative-path behavior across sandbox capabilities.

The SDK currently supports sharing one live sandbox session, but every run uses the session-wide `Manifest.root` for filesystem path resolution:

- `exec_command(workdir=...)` changes the directory for that shell command only.
- `view_image("plot.png")` resolves from the session workspace root.
- `apply_patch` paths are workspace-root-relative, not relative to the shell `workdir`.
- `run_as` changes the OS identity and permissions, but not path resolution.

This behavior is documented, so I am filing this as a feature request rather than a bug.

Relevant current behavior:

- [`exec_command` implements `workdir` as a per-command `cd`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/1816d2e9f93a0d7265094ec3c9c6c312ae5c3aff/src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/shell_tool.py#L70-L77)
- [`view_image` uses the session-wide workspace path policy](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/1816d2e9f93a0d7265094ec3c9c6c312ae5c3aff/src/agents/sandbox/capabilities/tools/view_image.py#L104-L113)
- [`SandboxRunConfig` has no run-level cwd or workspace view](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/1816d2e9f93a0d7265094ec3c9c6c312ae5c3aff/src/agents/run_config.py#L189-L219)
- The [Sandbox Agents guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes) notes that `apply_patch` paths are relative to the workspace root rather than shell `workdir`.

#### Production use case

Our application runs several trusted document-research agents concurrently. They share the same dependencies and do not require separate containers or security-grade isolation. Each agent only needs a reliable task-local directory:

```text
/workspace/tasks/task-a
/workspace/tasks/task-b
```

We originally reused one Modal sandbox and assigned each child a task directory. This produced two related problems:

1. Concurrent children sometimes chose identical workspace-root-relative filenames and overwrote or read each other's files.
2. After forcing each child's shell commands into its task directory, filesystem capabilities still used the session root.

For example:

```text
exec_command(
    cmd="render input.pdf --output page.png",
    workdir="tasks/task-a",
)

view_image(path="page.png")
# Looks for /workspace/page.png rather than
# /workspace/tasks/task-a/page.png.

apply_patch(path="notes.md", ...)
# Edits /workspace/notes.md rather than
# /workspace/tasks/task-a/notes.md.
```

We worked around this with capability-specific path-prefixing adapters, task-local temporary directories, and prompt instructions. That remained brittle because every path-bearing capability or custom tool had to implement the convention independently.

We eventually moved to one fresh Modal sandbox per child. That is reliable, but concurrent fan-out now multiplies sandbox startup overhead and active sandbox usage, and we sometimes approach our provider concurrency limits.

#### Desired behavior

The exact API is not important, but an illustrative shape might be:

```python
run_a = RunConfig(
    sandbox=SandboxRunConfig(

```

For `run_a`:

- shell commands without an explicit `workdir` start under `tasks/task-a`;
- a relative shell `workdir` is interpreted beneath `tasks/task-a`;
- `view_image("page.png")` reads `tasks/task-a/page.png`;
- an `apply_patch` operation on `notes.md` edits `tasks/task-a/notes.md`.

The scope should be bound to the run or its prepared capabilities, rather than implemented by mutating session-global cwd or path-policy state. That matters when multiple runs share the session concurrently.

Other desirable properties:

- Omitting `cwd` preserves current behavior.
- `Manifest.root`, session lifecycle, snapshots, and direct `BaseSandboxSession` operations remain session-scoped.
- `run_as` and filesystem permissions remain orthogonal and continue to compose with the path scope.
- Built-in workspace-backed capabilities have one consistent relative-path base.
- The design can support distinct scopes for concurrent runs sharing one developer-owned session.

#### Non-goals

- This does not need to be a chroot or security boundary.
- It does not replace separate sandboxes for untrusted agents, different images, or genuine compute isolation.
- It does not require per-run mounts, users, groups, or environments.
- It does not address child-agent orchestration or result delivery.
- Deliberate access through absolute paths or `..` could remain a separate policy decision; the immediate need is consistent handling of relative paths.

+def resolve_path_from_cwd(path: str | PurePath, cwd: str | PurePath | None) -> str | PurePath:
+    """Return ``path`` with a relative path re-based beneath a run-scoped ``cwd``.
+
+    ``cwd`` is interpreted the same way as any other workspace path: relative values are
+    relative to the workspace root. Absolute paths (POSIX or Windows) and calls without a
+    ``cwd`` are returned unchanged, so the session path policy still decides whether the final
+    path is allowed.
+    """
+
+    if cwd is None or windows_absolute_path(path) is not None:
+        return path
+    posix_path = coerce_posix_path(path)
+    if posix_path.is_absolute():
+        return path
+    return (coerce_posix_path(cwd) / posix_path).as_posix()

+"""Run two trusted agents in separate working directories of one live sandbox.
+
+Run-scoped working directories make relative paths consistent; they are not confinement.
+Use separate sandbox sessions for untrusted agents or workloads that need compute isolation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import base64
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from agents import ModelSettings, Runner, RunResult, ToolOutputImage
+from agents.items import ToolCallItem, ToolCallOutputItem
+from agents.run import RunConfig
+from agents.sandbox import Manifest, SandboxAgent, SandboxRunConfig
+from agents.sandbox.capabilities import Filesystem, Shell
+from agents.sandbox.entries import BaseEntry, Dir, File
+from agents.sandbox.sandboxes.unix_local import UnixLocalSandboxClient
+from agents.sandbox.session import BaseSandboxSession
+
+
+async def main(*, model: str) -> None:
+    client = UnixLocalSandboxClient()
+    agent_a = _build_agent(name="Task A worker", model=model)
+    agent_b = _build_agent(name="Task B worker", model=model)
+    shared_sandbox = await client.create(manifest=_build_manifest())
+
+    try:
+        # The session is shared, but each run gets a different base for relative paths.
+        run_a_config = RunConfig(
+            sandbox=SandboxRunConfig(
+                session=shared_sandbox,
+                cwd="tasks/task-a",
+            ),
+            workflow_name="Shared sandbox task A",
+        )
+        run_b_config = RunConfig(
+            sandbox=SandboxRunConfig(
+                session=shared_sandbox,
+                cwd="tasks/task-b",
+            ),
+            workflow_name="Shared sandbox task B",
+        )
+
+        async with shared_sandbox:
+            run_tasks = [
+                asyncio.create_task(
+                    Runner.run(
+                        agent_a,
+                        _task_prompt("task-a"),
+                        run_config=run_a_config,
+                        max_turns=10,
+                    )
+                ),
+                asyncio.create_task(
+                    Runner.run(
+                        agent_b,
+                        _task_prompt("task-b"),
+                        run_config=run_b_config,
+                        max_turns=10,
+                    )
+                ),
+            ]
+            result_a, result_b = await _run_concurrently(run_tasks)
+
+            # These checks make the demo self-verifying; applications do not need them.
+            await _verify_task(shared_sandbox, task_name="task-a", result=result_a)
+            await _verify_task(shared_sandbox, task_name="task-b", result=result_b)
+    finally:
+        await client.delete(shared_sandbox)
+
+    print("\nVerified: distinct run-scoped cwd values worked without session-global cwd mutation.")
+
+
+# Demo setup. Applications can create task directories and inputs however they prefer.
+
+DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-5.6-sol"
+
+# The two task directories intentionally contain the same relative filenames.
+TASKS = {
+    "task-a": (
+        "red",
+        "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAACAAAAAgCAIAAAD8GO2jAAAAKklEQVR4nGO4o6ZGU8QwasGoBaMWjFowasGoBaMWjFowasGoBaMWDBULAIjyoD0k0I5JAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC",
+    ),
+    "task-b": (
+        "blue",
+        "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAACAAAAAgCAIAAAD8GO2jAAAAKklEQVR4nGNQTX5NU8QwasGoBaMWjFowasGoBaMWjFowasGoBaMWDBULAMMtzEwilX6gAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC",
+    ),
+}
+
+SHELL_COMMAND = "cp reference.png page.png && cat brief.md"
+
+
+def _task_prompt(task_name: str) -> str:
+    return f"""
+Complete {task_name} in your current run working directory. Use only these relative paths:
+
+1. Call `exec_command` with `{SHELL_COMMAND}`. Do not pass `workdir`.
+2. Call `view_image` with `page.png` and identify its color.
+3. Use `apply_patch` on `notes.md` to change only `status=pending-{task_name}` to
+   `status=complete-{task_name}`.
+4. Reply with the task name and image color from the files you inspected.
+
+Do not prefix paths with `tasks/`, use absolute paths, or use the shell to edit `notes.md`.
+""".strip()
+
+
+def _build_manifest() -> Manifest:
+    task_dirs: dict[str | Path, BaseEntry] = {}
+    for task_name, (color, image_base64) in TASKS.items():
+        task_dirs[task_name] = Dir(
+            children={
+                "brief.md": File(
+                    content=f"# {task_name}\n\nThe reference image is {color}.\n".encode()
+                ),
+                "reference.png": File(content=base64.b64decode(image_base64)),
+                "notes.md": File(
+                    content=f"task={task_name}\nstatus=pending-{task_name}\n".encode()
+                ),
+            }
+        )
+    return Manifest(entries={"tasks": Dir(children=task_dirs)})
+
+
+def _build_agent(*, name: str, model: str) -> SandboxAgent:
+    # These settings only make the demo's dependent tool sequence deterministic.
+    # Run-scoped cwd does not require them.
+    return SandboxAgent(
+        name=name,
+        model=model,
+        instructions=(

+            "the base for every relative path."
+        ),
+        capabilities=[Shell(), Filesystem()],
+        model_settings=ModelSettings(tool_choice="required", parallel_tool_calls=False),
+    )

+async def _run_concurrently(
+    run_tasks: list[asyncio.Task[RunResult]],
+) -> tuple[RunResult, RunResult]:
+    """Keep both runs terminal before the caller closes their shared session."""
+    try:
+        result_a, result_b = await asyncio.gather(*run_tasks)
+    except BaseException:
+        for run_task in run_tasks:
+            if not run_task.done():
+                run_task.cancel()
+        await asyncio.gather(*run_tasks, return_exceptions=True)
+        raise
+    return result_a, result_b
+
+
+# Demo verification. Applications do not need to inspect raw tool calls this way.
+
+
+def _tool_call_name(item: ToolCallItem) -> str:
+    raw_item = item.raw_item
+    if isinstance(raw_item, dict):
+        type_name = raw_item.get("type")
+        name = raw_item.get("name")
+    else:
+        type_name = getattr(raw_item, "type", None)
+        name = getattr(raw_item, "name", None)
+
+    if type_name == "apply_patch_call":
+        return "apply_patch"
+    if isinstance(name, str):
+        return name
+    return type_name if isinstance(type_name, str) else ""
+
+
+def _function_call_arguments(item: ToolCallItem) -> dict[str, object]:
+    raw_item = item.raw_item
+    if isinstance(raw_item, dict):
+        arguments = raw_item.get("arguments")
+    else:
+        arguments = getattr(raw_item, "arguments", None)
+    if not isinstance(arguments, str):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{_tool_call_name(item)} did not provide JSON arguments")
+
+    try:
+        parsed = json.loads(arguments)
+    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{_tool_call_name(item)} provided invalid JSON arguments") from error
+    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{_tool_call_name(item)} arguments were not an object")
+    return parsed
+
+
+def _apply_patch_input(item: ToolCallItem) -> str:
+    raw_item = item.raw_item
+    if isinstance(raw_item, dict):
+        raw_input = raw_item.get("input")
+    else:
+        raw_input = getattr(raw_item, "input", None)
+    if not isinstance(raw_input, str):
+        raise RuntimeError("apply_patch did not provide patch input")
+    return raw_input
