+
+
+@function_tool(name_override="write_other", needs_approval=True)
+def write_other(query: str) -> str:
+    return f"other:{query}"
+
+
+@function_tool(name_override="look_up", needs_approval=False)
+def look_up(query: str) -> str:
+    return f"schema for {query}"
+
+
+@output_guardrail
+async def always_fine(
+    ctx: RunContextWrapper[object], agent: AgentType[object], output: object
+) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:
+    return GuardrailFunctionOutput(output_info=None, tripwire_triggered=False)
+
+
+@output_guardrail
+async def always_trips(
+    ctx: RunContextWrapper[object], agent: AgentType[object], output: object
+) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:
+    return GuardrailFunctionOutput(output_info=None, tripwire_triggered=True)
+
+
+@output_guardrail
+async def always_crashes(
+    ctx: RunContextWrapper[object], agent: AgentType[object], output: object
+) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:
+    raise RuntimeError("guardrail crashed")
+
+
+_DEFERRING_BEHAVIOR = StopAtTools(stop_at_tool_names=["finish"])
+
+
+def _make_deferring_agent(
+    tool_use_behavior: StopAtTools | Literal["run_llm_again"] = _DEFERRING_BEHAVIOR,
+) -> Agent:
+    """A gated write on the second model turn, so the resumed boundary has a prefix."""
+    return Agent(
+        name="deferred repro",
+        instructions="Always call write_thing.",
+        model=ScriptedModel(
+            [
+                ModelStep(output=[function_call("look_up", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_LOOKUP")]),
+                ModelStep(
+                    output=[function_call("write_thing", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED")]
+                ),
+                ModelStep(output=[assistant_message("done")]),
+            ]
+        ),
+        tools=[look_up, write_thing],
+        output_guardrails=[always_fine],
+        tool_use_behavior=tool_use_behavior,
+    )
+
+
+def _make_multi_approval_agent(
+    tool_use_behavior: StopAtTools | Literal["run_llm_again"] = _DEFERRING_BEHAVIOR,
+) -> Agent:
+    """One deferred model response carrying two approval-required calls."""
+    return Agent(
+        name="deferred repro (multi)",
+        instructions="Call both tools.",
+        model=ScriptedModel(
+            [
+                ModelStep(
+                    output=[
+                        function_call("write_thing", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED"),
+                        function_call("write_other", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED_2"),
+                    ]
+                ),
+                ModelStep(output=[assistant_message("done")]),
+            ]
+        ),
+        tools=[write_thing, write_other],
+        output_guardrails=[always_fine],
+        tool_use_behavior=tool_use_behavior,
+    )
+
+
+_PREAMBLE_TEXT = "About to write the thing."
+
+
+def _make_terminal_tool_agent(
+    *,
+    with_guardrails: bool = True,
+    tripping: bool = False,
+    crashing: bool = False,
+    with_preamble: bool = False,
+) -> Agent:
+    """The approved tool is terminal, so the resume ends in a final output."""
+    guardrails = [always_fine]
+    if tripping:
+        guardrails = [always_trips]
+    if crashing:
+        guardrails = [always_crashes]
+    parked_response = [function_call("write_thing", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED")]
+    if with_preamble:
+        parked_response = [assistant_message(_PREAMBLE_TEXT), *parked_response]
+    return Agent(
+        name="deferred repro (terminal)",
+        instructions="Always call write_thing.",
+        model=ScriptedModel(
+            [
+                ModelStep(output=[function_call("look_up", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_LOOKUP")]),
+                ModelStep(output=parked_response),
+            ]
+        ),
+        tools=[look_up, write_thing],
+        output_guardrails=guardrails if with_guardrails else [],
+        tool_use_behavior=StopAtTools(stop_at_tool_names=["write_thing"]),
+    )
+
+
+def _make_partial_filter_handoff_agent() -> Agent:
+    """Two gated calls plus a handoff whose filter drops exactly one resolved output.
+
+    An ``input_filter`` is an arbitrary caller callable, so dropping a subset of the
+    resolved outputs is a legitimate shape; the held batch must not settle a call whose
+    output the filter took away.
+    """
+    from agents import HandoffInputData, handoff
+
+    def drops_one_output(data: HandoffInputData) -> HandoffInputData:
+        def keep(items: tuple) -> tuple:
+            kept = []
+            for item in items:
+                raw = getattr(item, "raw_item", None)
+                call_id = (
+                    raw.get("call_id") if isinstance(raw, dict) else getattr(raw, "call_id", None)
+                )
+                if call_id == "call_PARKED_2" and item.type == "tool_call_output_item":
+                    continue
+                kept.append(item)
+            return tuple(kept)
+
+        return HandoffInputData(
+            input_history=data.input_history,
+            pre_handoff_items=keep(data.pre_handoff_items),
+            new_items=keep(data.new_items),
+        )
+
+    target = Agent(
+        name="target",
+        instructions="x",
+        model=ScriptedModel([ModelStep(output=[assistant_message("done")])]),
+    )
+    return Agent(
+        name="deferred repro (partial filter)",
+        instructions="x",
+        model=ScriptedModel(
+            [
+                ModelStep(
+                    output=[
+                        function_call("write_thing", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED"),
+                        function_call("write_other", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED_2"),
+                        function_call("transfer_to_target", {}, call_id="call_HANDOFF"),
+                    ]
+                ),
+                ModelStep(output=[assistant_message("done")]),
+            ]
+        ),
+        tools=[write_thing, write_other],
+        handoffs=[handoff(target, input_filter=drops_one_output)],
+        output_guardrails=[always_fine],
+        tool_use_behavior=_DEFERRING_BEHAVIOR,
+    )
+
+
+class _FailingResumeSession(SimpleListSession):
+    """Control append acknowledgement at the public Session boundary."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.failure: str | None = None
+        self.error = RuntimeError("session append failed")
+
+    async def add_items(self, items: list[TResponseInputItem]) -> None:
+        failure, self.failure = self.failure, None
+        if failure == "before":
+            raise self.error
+        await super().add_items(items)
+        if failure == "after":
+            raise self.error
+
+
+async def _run(
+    agent: Agent, run_input: Any, session: Any, *, streamed: bool
+) -> RunResult | RunResultStreaming:
+    if streamed:
+        result = Runner.run_streamed(agent, run_input, session=session)
+        async for _ in result.stream_events():
+            pass
+        return result
+    return await Runner.run(agent, run_input, session=session)
+
+
+async def _serialized_round_trip(result: RunResult | RunResultStreaming, agent: Agent) -> RunState:
+    return await RunState.from_json(agent, json.loads(json.dumps(result.to_state().to_json())))
+
+
+def _held_write(items: Any) -> Any:
+    return {
+        "session_id": "test",
+        "items": items,
+        "before": None,
+        "persisted_count": 0,
+        "held": True,
+        "current_response": {"turn": 0, "start": 0},
+    }
+
+
+def _call_ids(items: list[TResponseInputItem]) -> list[Any]:
+    return [item.get("call_id") for item in items if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
+
+
+def _orphaned_outputs(items: list[TResponseInputItem]) -> list[Any]:
+    calls = set(_call_ids(items))
+    return [
+        item.get("call_id")
+        for item in items
+        if item.get("type") == "function_call_output" and item.get("call_id") not in calls
+    ]
+
+
+def _parked_pair(items: list[TResponseInputItem]) -> list[str]:
+    return [
+        str(item.get("type"))
+        for item in items
+        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("call_id") == "call_PARKED"
+    ]
+
+
+async def _parked_and_approved(
+    agent: Agent, session: Any, *, streamed: bool, resume_agent: Agent | None = None

+    assert len(first.interruptions) == 1
+    state = await _serialized_round_trip(first, resume_agent or agent)
+    state.approve(state.get_interruptions()[0])
+    return state
+

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_the_compaction_deferral_reads_the_settling_batch_not_the_callers_input() -> None:
+    # The batch settles through ``original_input``, so the deferral has to look there;
+    # but that slot also carries the caller's own turn input on every ordinary

+
+    session = _CompactionRecordingSession()
+    held: list[TResponseInputItem] = [

+        {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_PARKED", "output": "ok"},

+def test_the_pairing_guard_speaks_every_approval_identity() -> None:
+    # A hosted MCP approval request identifies itself with ``id`` and its response
+    # points back with ``approval_request_id``; custom calls pair by ``call_id``. A
+    # request kind the guard cannot key would settle alone and poison the Session the
+    # same way an unpaired function call does.
+    from agents.run_internal.session_persistence import _held_items_safe_to_settle
+
+    unpaired_mcp: TResponseInputItem = {
+        "type": "mcp_approval_request",
+        "id": "mcpr_1",
+        "name": "do_it",
+        "server_label": "srv",
+        "arguments": "{}",
+    }
+    paired_mcp: TResponseInputItem = {
+        "type": "mcp_approval_request",
+        "id": "mcpr_2",
+        "name": "do_it",
+        "server_label": "srv",
+        "arguments": "{}",
+    }
+    mcp_response: TResponseInputItem = {
+        "type": "mcp_approval_response",
+        "approval_request_id": "mcpr_2",
+        "approve": True,
+    }
+    unpaired_custom: TResponseInputItem = {
+        "type": "custom_tool_call",
+        "call_id": "cust_1",
+        "name": "custom",
+        "input": "",
+    }
+    preamble: TResponseInputItem = {"role": "assistant", "content": "hi", "type": "message"}
+
+    kept = _held_items_safe_to_settle(
+        [unpaired_mcp, paired_mcp, mcp_response, unpaired_custom, preamble], [], None
+    )

+
+    still_pending = _held_items_safe_to_settle(
+        [unpaired_mcp], [], None, pending_call_ids={"mcpr_1"}

+    # emits the version that introduced the keys, loads under that label, and is refused

+    await RunState.from_json(agent, json.loads(json.dumps(payload)))

+    relabeled = json.loads(json.dumps(payload))
+    relabeled["$schemaVersion"] = "1.18"
+    with pytest.raises(UserError, match="pending Session write is invalid"):

+    async def clear_session(self, *, wrapper: RunContextWrapper[Any] | None = None) -> None:

+    # pairing contract applies: the filtered call must not land dangling. Cancellation
+    # only exists on the streaming runner, and this checkpoint shape resumes from the
+    # live state.

+    detached = Runner.run_streamed(agent, state, session=None)

+    async for _ in detached.stream_events():
+        pass

+    async for _ in reattached.stream_events():

+def _make_deferring_agent_with_a_turn_after_the_resume() -> Agent:
+    """A gated write whose resume runs one more model turn before finishing.

+    The extra turn moves the final output past the resumed boundary and onto the main
+    loop, which owns its own detached-completion disposal.
+    """
+    return Agent(
+        name="deferred repro (turn after resume)",
+        instructions="Always call write_thing.",
+        model=ScriptedModel(
+            [
+                ModelStep(output=[function_call("look_up", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_LOOKUP")]),
+                ModelStep(
+                    output=[function_call("write_thing", {"query": "x"}, call_id="call_PARKED")]
+                ),
+                ModelStep(output=[function_call("look_up", {"query": "y"}, call_id="call_AFTER")]),
+                ModelStep(output=[assistant_message("done")]),
+            ]
+        ),
+        tools=[look_up, write_thing],
+        output_guardrails=[always_fine],

+    ids=["final-on-the-resumed-turn", "final-on-a-later-turn"],
+)
+async def test_a_failed_detached_completion_keeps_the_held_record(
+    streamed: bool, make_agent: Callable[[], Agent]
+) -> None:
+    # A detached completion discards the batch because the run ends there, but only
+    # once it has ended: the guardrails and the final save run after the terminal step
+    # is chosen, and a failure there leaves a checkpoint whose reattach is the batch's
+    # only remaining way into the Session.
+
+    @output_guardrail
+    async def _fails(ctx: Any, agent: Agent, output: Any) -> GuardrailFunctionOutput:
+        raise RuntimeError("output guardrail failed")
+
+    session = SimpleListSession()
+    agent = make_agent()
+    state = await _parked_and_approved(agent, session, streamed=streamed)
+    assert state._pending_session_write is not None
+    agent.output_guardrails = [*agent.output_guardrails, _fails]
+
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+        await _run(agent, state, None, streamed=streamed)
+
+    assert state._pending_session_write is not None

title: BackendSpanExporter drops the whole batch on HTTP 429 instead of retrying with Retry-After

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause the same way: 408/409/429 join the retry path, Retry-After / retry-after-ms are parsed with the existing agents.models._retry_runtime helpers, and the wait is bounded by max_delay. The independent tests confirm both deliver the batch on retry, stop at max_retries, honour both headers, cap large values, and leave other 4xx non-retried. The difference is scope and craft. Patch B is a tight change: a module constant, a small helper that reuses the existing header_lookup utility (case-insensitive, None-safe), and `max(backoff, min(retry_after, max_delay))` which matches the issue's wording exactly while leaving the existing backoff/jitter untouched. Its tests cover retry, give-up at max_retries, header precedence (ms over seconds), the max_delay bound, and the deadline interaction (a 30s Retry-After against a 5s drain deadline is cut at the deadline), all of which fail on base. Parsing Retry-After on 5xx too is a small, low-risk extension. Patch A does the core fix correctly but bundles unrelated work: it introduces new `x-should-retry: false` semantics that change existing 5xx behaviour (a 503 with that header is now dropped instead of retried), rewrites `_sleep_before_retry` in a way that is behaviourally equivalent to the old code (pure churn in the deadline path), adds a timed-shutdown drain test that would already pass on base since the deadline branch never consulted the shutdown event, and edits an existing test's patch target for no functional reason. The lazy import with a 'must not become an import-time dependency' comment is unsupported given B's top-level import works in the harness. A's `min(max(sleep, retry_after), max_delay)` also silently clips jitter above max_delay only when a header is present, an inconsistent side effect. A's tests are fine (including unparsable/negative cases), but the extra behaviour change on 5xx and the unrelated refactor add risk and obscure the fix, so B is the better patch.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes: [Tracing](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/) and the `BackendSpanExporter` reference.
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #4683 / #4711 cover retries being disabled after shutdown, #4983 covers a non-serializable value dropping a batch, #5008 covers the endpoint. None covers how the exporter classifies HTTP status codes.

### Describe the bug

`BackendSpanExporter._export_with_deadline()` treats every `4xx` response as final:

```python
# If the response is a client error (4xx), we won't retry
if 400 <= response.status_code < 500:
    logger.error("[non-fatal] Tracing client error %s: %s", ...)
    break
```

That includes `429 Too Many Requests`. A single rate-limited response from `/v1/traces/ingest` discards the whole batch, up to `max_batch_size` (128) traces and spans, with no retry and without looking at `Retry-After`. The run itself succeeds, so the only symptom is a gap in the dashboard and one `[non-fatal]` log line. The same applies to `408` and `409`, which the OpenAI Python client (`_base_client._should_retry`) retries together with `429` and `5xx`; the exporter only mirrors the `5xx` half of that policy.

The export path already has everything needed to retry: `max_retries`, `base_delay`, `max_delay`, the backoff loop, and `agents.models._retry_runtime.parse_retry_after_value` / `parse_retry_after_ms` for the header.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` at `fbf59a40` (also 0.22.0)
- Python version: 3.10.12
- Operating system: Linux
- Model and model provider: none needed; `httpx2.Client` is patched
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently for any 429

```text
ERROR:openai.agents:[non-fatal] Tracing client error 429. Response data is redacted.
post calls: 1
```

### Repro steps

```python
import logging
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from agents.tracing.processors import BackendSpanExporter
from agents.tracing.spans import SpanImpl
from agents.tracing.span_data import CustomSpanData

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

with patch("httpx2.Client") as client:
    limited = MagicMock(status_code=429, headers={"retry-after": "1"})
    limited.text = '{"error": {"message": "Rate limit reached"}}'
    ok = MagicMock(status_code=200)
    client.return_value.post.side_effect = [limited, ok]

    exporter = BackendSpanExporter(api_key="sk-test", max_retries=3, base_delay=0.1)
    span = SpanImpl(
        trace_id="trace_1",
        span_id="span_1",
        parent_id=None,
        processor=MagicMock(),
        span_data=CustomSpanData(name="probe", data={}),
        tracing_api_key=None,
    )
    exporter.export([span])
    print("post calls:", client.return_value.post.call_count)  # 1: the batch is gone
```

### Expected behavior

`408`, `409` and `429` are retried with the existing backoff up to `max_retries`, waiting at least the advertised `Retry-After` / `retry-after-ms` (bounded by `max_delay`), the way the OpenAI client and the SDK's own model retry helpers already treat these statuses. Other `4xx` responses stay non-retried. In the script above the second call succeeds and `post calls` is 2.

A fix with regression tests is ready and I will attach it right away.

title: Cancelling a MCP server work task does not stop the worker

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the independent test pass and preserve the CancelledServer contract, so the decision rests on root-cause fidelity and risk.

Patch B follows the design the issue itself sketches: on 3.11+ it uses the official `Task.cancelling()` signal, on 3.10 it substitutes a `Task` subclass that counts cancel requests and resets per command, and it adds the missing `uncancel()` to the fallback timeout path in `_run_with_timeout_in_task` so that path no longer leaves a stale request behind. It also handles the case where the command swallows the external cancellation (post-command `cancelling()` check), settles queued commands in a `finally`, and refuses new commands once the task is done (`_enqueue`). Because it relies on `cancelling()` on 3.11+, it correctly ignores anyio-style internal cancel/uncancel cycles that the real MCP transports perform. Its tests cover external cancel, swallowed cancel, queued commands, manager bookkeeping, CancelledServer, the pre-3.11 fallback timeout path, and anyio-like self-cancellation; the one skipped test is skipped only where the behaviour is genuinely undetectable (pre-3.11), and the core tests run everywhere.

Patch A instead hooks the loop's task factory to monkeypatch `task.cancel` on the instance and counts every cancel() call even on 3.11+, ignoring `cancelling()`/`uncancel()`. That counter is perturbed by any library that cancels the host task internally (anyio `fail_after`, task groups, which the MCP SDK uses), so a server-raised CancelledError that follows such internal activity would be misclassified as external and kill the worker, the exact distinction the issue asks to preserve. It does not handle a command that swallows the external cancellation, so that case reproduces the original hang. It also widens scope considerably: a new required constructor argument on `_ServerWorker`, temporary replacement of the loop's task factory, and an 'emergency cleanup' run inside the cancelled task. That cleanup is bounded only by `cleanup_timeout_seconds`; if that is None and cleanup hangs, the cancelled worker again never finishes, re-creating the issue's symptom. These additions add risk without being required by the issue.

B resolves the root cause more faithfully, with less risk and well-targeted tests; A's extra machinery introduces new misclassification and hang paths.

issue_md:
### Describe the bug

Cancelling a `_ServerWorker` task does not stop the worker. `_ServerWorker._run`
(`src/agents/mcp/manager.py:93-110`) wraps the command it is running in `except BaseException`, records the
error on the command's future and continues its loop. `asyncio.CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so an
external cancellation is consumed as if it were a command failure and the worker goes back to
`await self._queue.get()`.

The task stays alive in the `cancelling` state, so `is_done` stays `False`, the manager's
`add_done_callback` / `_handle_worker_done` bookkeeping never runs, and anything awaiting the task (including
loop shutdown) waits for a task that will not finish.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` @ `fbf59a40`
- Python version: 3.14.0

### Repro steps

```python
import asyncio
from typing import Any, cast

from agents.mcp.manager import _ServerWorker


class _BlockingServer:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.connect_started = asyncio.Event()

    async def connect(self) -> None:
        self.connect_started.set()
        await asyncio.sleep(3600)

    async def cleanup(self) -> None:
        return None


async def test_cancelling_the_worker_task_stops_the_worker() -> None:
    server = _BlockingServer()
    worker = _ServerWorker(cast(Any, server))

    caller = asyncio.create_task(worker.connect(timeout_seconds=None))
    await asyncio.wait_for(server.connect_started.wait(), timeout=1)

    worker._task.cancel()
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)

    caller.cancel()
    try:
        await caller
    except BaseException:
        pass

    assert worker._task.done(), "the worker task survived cancellation and is still looping"
```

Result on `main`:

```
AssertionError: the worker task survived cancellation and is still looping
<Task cancelling name='Task-2' coro=<_ServerWorker._run() running at src/agents/mcp/manager.py:95>
```

### Expected behavior

Cancelling the worker task ends it.

### Why this is not a one-line re-raise

A server's own `connect`/`cleanup` may raise `CancelledError` deliberately — `CancelledServer` in
`tests/mcp/test_mcp_server_manager.py`, together with `suppress_cancelled_error`, depends on that error
reaching the caller through the command future. So the two cases need separating: an error raised *by the
command* (settle the future, keep looping) versus a cancellation *of the worker itself* (settle the future,
then stop).

`asyncio.current_task().cancelling() > 0` distinguishes them on 3.11+, but the fallback timeout path in
`_run_with_timeout_in_task` (`manager.py:135-148`) calls `task.cancel()` and converts the result to
`TimeoutError` without a matching `uncancel()`, which would leave a pending cancellation request behind on
that path. `cancelling()` also does not exist on 3.10, which the project still supports.

Happy to send a PR with tests once you decide which behaviour you want.

title: Realtime: agent_end names the post-handoff agent instead of the agent whose turn ended

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the identical core fix: in the turn_ended branch they capture `self._active_output_response_agent or self._current_agent` before the guardrail state is cleared and pass it to RealtimeAgentEndEvent. This is exactly the root cause the issue identifies (the snapshot taken at turn_started is the agent that produced the turn, and it was being cleared one line before the end event was built). All five independent tests fail on base and pass on both patches, so on the issue's core scenarios they are equivalent.

The differences are in tests and in one adjacent change. Patch A adds a single test that mirrors the repro (start A, handoff A->B, end A, and asserts `_current_agent` is B). Patch B adds two tests: one that also drives the follow-up turn and asserts the full paired sequence (start A, handoff, end A, start B, end B), which directly exercises the per-agent pairing the issue says consumers depend on, and one for a late turn_started arriving after output and a handoff for the same response. Patch B's second source change makes agent_start use the same snapshot when turn_started arrives after the response was already activated by earlier output; in that ordering base would name B as the starter of A's response, the same misattribution class the issue describes, so the change is consistent with the fix and the guardrail precedent rather than unrelated churn, and it is covered by a test. It is low risk because a fresh response re-assigns the snapshot in the same branch.

Craft is a minor wash: A's test sits in test_session.py with top-level imports, while B uses function-local imports in a handoff test file, which is slightly less tidy. Overall B wins on test strength (verifies the next-turn pairing the issue motivates) with equal correctness on the reported bug and a coherent, low-risk adjacent consistency fix.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes.
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. No open or closed issue covers which agent `agent_end` names after an in-response handoff.

### Describe the bug

When a Realtime response contains a handoff tool call, the handoff completes before the model's `turn_ended` event and moves `_current_agent` to the target agent. The `turn_ended` branch in `RealtimeSession` then emits `RealtimeAgentEndEvent(agent=self._current_agent)`, so the caller sees:

```text
agent_start(A)  →  handoff(A → B)  →  agent_end(B)  →  agent_start(B)  →  agent_end(B)
```

`RealtimeAgentEndEvent.agent` is documented as "The agent that ended", but A never ends and B ends without having started. Any consumer that pairs `agent_start` / `agent_end` per agent (turn markers in a UI, per-agent timing, per-agent usage attribution read on `agent_end`) attributes A's turn to B.

The session already knows which agent produced the turn: `_active_output_response_agent` is captured at `turn_started` and is what the output guardrails use for the same reason. It is cleared one line before the `agent_end` event is built.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` at 58a6d2c9 (also present in v0.22.2)
- Python version: 3.12.13
- Operating system: macOS 15
- Model and model provider: any Realtime model; reproduced with `ScriptedRealtimeModel` from `agents.realtime.testing`
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently, whenever a handoff runs inside a response

### Repro steps

Self-contained, no network.

```python
import asyncio

from agents.realtime.agent import RealtimeAgent
from agents.realtime.events import RealtimeAgentEndEvent, RealtimeAgentStartEvent, RealtimeHandoffEvent
from agents.realtime.model_events import (
    RealtimeModelToolCallEvent,
    RealtimeModelTurnEndedEvent,
    RealtimeModelTurnStartedEvent,
)
from agents.realtime.session import RealtimeSession
from agents.realtime.testing import ScriptedRealtimeModel


async def main():
    agent_b = RealtimeAgent(name="b")
    agent_a = RealtimeAgent(name="a", handoffs=[agent_b])
    model = ScriptedRealtimeModel(strict=False)
    session = RealtimeSession(model, agent_a, None, run_config={"async_tool_calls": False})
    await session.enter()

    await model.emit(RealtimeModelTurnStartedEvent(response_id="response_1"))
    await model.emit(RealtimeModelToolCallEvent(name="transfer_to_b", call_id="call_1", arguments="{}"))
    await model.emit(RealtimeModelTurnEndedEvent(response_id="response_1"))

    while not session._event_queue.empty():
        event = session._event_queue.get_nowait()
        if isinstance(event, RealtimeAgentStartEvent):
            print("agent_start", event.agent.name)
        elif isinstance(event, RealtimeHandoffEvent):
            print("handoff", event.from_agent.name, "->", event.to_agent.name)
        elif isinstance(event, RealtimeAgentEndEvent):
```

title: Responses streaming: the `error` event is not treated as terminal, so a teardown failure masks the provider's error

judge.reasoning:
Both patches apply the identical root-cause fix: adding "error" to `_ResponseStreamWithRequestId._TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES`, which is exactly what the issue asks for, and both pass the independent tests (base FAIL-EXC with the masking RuntimeError, A and B PASS). Correctness on the reported scenario is therefore equal.

The difference is in scope and test quality. Patch A adds a second production change: a `break` out of the `async for` in `stream_response` once `terminal_failure_error` is set. With the terminal-set fix in place this is redundant (the next `__anext__` would hit `_cleanup_after_exhaustion`, which now debug-logs the teardown failure), so it is unrequested hardening that changes the post-terminal control flow for `response.failed`/`response.incomplete` as well as `error`: the stream is now closed via the explicit close path instead of being exhausted. Nothing in the issue motivates this, and it obscures which change actually fixes the bug. Patch B keeps the production change to the single line the issue identifies.

On tests, B adds a parametrised `_ResponseStreamWithRequestId` unit test over `error` and `response.failed` (fails on base for `error` with the RuntimeError, passes after) and an end-to-end `stream_response` test asserting the `ModelBehaviorError` carries the provider's code and message. These are focused, obviously runnable, and mirror the issue's own repro table. A's tests are broader (a parametrised rewrite of an existing test, a unit test, and a real httpx MockTransport SSE test with failing `aclose`), and the SSE-level test is attractive because it exercises real transport teardown. But it depends on an undefined-in-diff helper (`_response_with_terminal_status`) and on exact SDK SSE parsing of `event: error`, which cannot be confirmed here, and its `None` case locks in behaviour (teardown error surfacing when no terminal event) that the issue does not ask for. Since patch-authored test outcomes are not in evidence, A's extra coverage is unverified while B's is straightforward.

Net: equal correctness, adequate and precise tests on both sides, but A carries an unrequested behavioural change in the hot streaming loop and heavier, less certain tests. B is the cleaner fix for the issue as stated.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- Have you read the docs? Yes.
- Have you searched for related issues? Yes. Ten open pull requests, none touching `_TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES`; no open or closed issue naming the `error` stream event as non-terminal.

### Describe the bug

`_ResponseStreamWithRequestId._TERMINAL_EVENT_TYPES` at `src/agents/models/openai_responses.py:261` lists `"response.error"` but not `"error"`. The SDK's error event is `ResponseErrorEvent`, whose type is `Literal["error"]`:

```python
# openai/types/responses/response_error_event.py  (openai 3.0.0)
    type: Literal["error"]
    """The type of the event. Always `error`."""
```

So an error-terminated stream never sets `_yielded_terminal_event`. `_cleanup_after_exhaustion` then re-raises a transport teardown failure rather than debug-logging it. That teardown error escapes, and it masks the `ModelBehaviorError` built from the provider's own `code` and `message`.

The same file already holds the correct set. `stream_response` carries its own at `:761-767`, and that one lists both:

```python
if chunk_type in {
    "response.completed",
    "response.failed",
    "response.incomplete",
    "error",
    "response.error",
}:
```

One line brings `:261` into line with `:761`.

This is not a test-only path. `_ResponseStreamWithRequestId` is built at `:916` with `cleanup=lambda: api_response_cm.__aexit__(...)`, so the cleanup is a real httpx teardown.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: repository `main` at `588826c`
- Related library versions: `openai` 3.0.0 (the pin is `openai>=3.0.0,<4`)
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04
- Model and model provider: OpenAI Responses API, any model. The trigger is the provider emitting an `error` event, not a particular model.
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest release? Yes, on `main` at `588826c`.
- Does it occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently, whenever an `error` event arrives and the transport teardown then fails.

### Repro steps

Driving `_ResponseStreamWithRequestId` with a cleanup that raises, one working event type and one that does not:

```
event type           terminal_seen   what __anext__ raised
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
response.failed      True            StopAsyncIteration (cleanup error suppressed)
error                False           RuntimeError: transport close failed
```

End to end on the real `stream_response` path, with the provider emitting an `error` event and the teardown failing:

```
on main:      caller sees -> RuntimeError: transport close failed
with the fix: caller sees -> ModelBehaviorError: Responses stream ended with terminal
              event `error`. code=server_error; message=the provider gave up.
```

The first hides the diagnosis the provider sent behind a transport artefact.

### Expected behavior

An `error` event ends the stream, so the teardown failure is debug-logged and the `ModelBehaviorError` carrying the provider's `code` and `message` reaches the caller. That is what `response.failed` already does.

### One related place that is not a second instance

A third terminal set at `:1437-1442`, in the websocket `_stream_response`, also omits `"error"`. It is unreachable. `event_type == "error"` raises `ResponsesWebSocketError` at `:1426`, before that set is read. I left it alone.

### Offer

`CONTRIBUTING.md` limits pull requests to collaborators and asks non-collaborators to open an issue, so this is an issue. The fix is written and verified locally all the same. One line in `openai_responses.py`, plus one parametrised test beside the existing `_ResponseStreamWithRequestId` cleanup tests.

```
uv run ruff format --check   → 994 files already formatted
uv run ruff check            → All checks passed!
uv run mypy src              → Success: no issues found in 317 source files
pyright                      → 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
pytest -n 8 -m "not serial"  → 11209 passed, 29 skipped
run_serial_tests.py          → 77 passed, 4 skipped, 77 deselected
.agents/skills/code-change-verification/scripts/run.sh → all commands passed
```

Baseline on unmodified `main` is `11207 passed, 29 skipped`, so the delta is exactly the two new cases. Falsification, with the production file reverted and the test kept: the `[error]` case fails with `RuntimeError: transport close failed`, and the `[response.failed]` control still passes.

Say the word and I will open the pull request, or take the one line as it stands.

title: Voice: add_audio(None) doesn't end the STT session, so the pipeline waits ~1000s for EVENT_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT

judge.reasoning: Both patches send a final commit, tolerate the empty-buffer error, and wait for outstanding transcripts, but they differ in how the session actually ends. Patch B's `_finish_input` commits only when server VAD reported uncommitted speech, waits for pending `committed` items to get their transcripts (bounded by a 10 s deadline plus a 0.3 s quiet-period), and then closes the websocket itself so `_handle_events` receives `WebsocketDoneSentinel`. This is exactly the shape the issue proposes and does not depend on the server replying to anything after end of input. Patch A instead unconditionally sends `commit` + `clear` from inside `_handle_events` and only breaks once it has seen `input_audio_buffer.cleared` and all pending transcripts; it never closes the socket on its own. If the server does not answer the clear (the issue's own repro server, or any deviation in error code / event_id matching), A falls back to the full 1000 s `EVENT_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT` and then raises an error, which is the very symptom the issue reports plus a new failure. The independent repro-server test confirms this: A still hangs past 5 s while B passes; A passes the four tests where the fake server cooperates. A also widens behaviour in risky ways beyond the ask: any `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.failed` event now kills the whole session (previously ignored, and this applies mid-session, not just at EOF), and a server-side close after EOF becomes a hard error unless `close()` was called. B's additions are confined to end-of-input bookkeeping; its main cost is a small fixed 0.3 s grace delay on every EOF and reliance on `speech_started` to decide whether to commit, which matches the issue's suggested condition. On tests, both add real websocket-server tests through the public pipeline that would fail on base (the stream would hang) and pass after; A's matrix is broader but is tailored to A's commit/clear handshake. Correctness and robustness favour B decisively.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes.
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #1686 / #1687 documented `None` as the end-of-stream signal. #4995, #4259, #4825 and #4343 cover close during setup, dispatcher start, cancellation and close errors, not end of input.

### Describe the bug

`StreamedAudioInput.add_audio(None)` is documented as "indicates the end of the stream". With `OpenAISTTModel`, the pipeline doesn't actually end: `result.stream()` keeps waiting for about 16.7 minutes and the STT websocket stays open.

In `src/agents/voice/models/openai_stt.py`, `_stream_audio` just `break`s when it reads `None`. It sends no `input_audio_buffer.commit`, doesn't close the websocket, and doesn't tell `_handle_events`. After that, nothing on the client side ends the session:

- `_handle_events` finishes only on `WebsocketDoneSentinel` (socket closed) or after `EVENT_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT = 1000` seconds without events.
- So `transcribe_turns()` doesn't finish, `_run_multi_turn` never reaches `output._done()`, and `session_ended` is never emitted.

Consequences:

1. `async for event in result.stream()` hangs for ~1000 s after the caller has said the input is over, and the websocket stays open for that time.
2. Because no commit is sent, a final utterance that server VAD hasn't closed yet (for example push-to-talk released mid-phrase) is never transcribed.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: `main` at c467732e
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: macOS 15
- Model: `gpt-4o-transcribe` via `OpenAISTTModel`; reproduced against a fake websocket, no network

### Repro steps

A fake server acknowledges the session, transcribes one turn and keeps the socket open. TTS is a stub.

<details><summary>Repro script</summary>

```python

class FakeServerWS:
    def __init__(self):
        self.incoming: asyncio.Queue[str] = asyncio.Queue()
        self.sent: list[dict] = []
        self.closed = asyncio.Event()
        self.incoming.put_nowait(json.dumps({"type": "session.created"}))

    async def __aenter__(self): return self
    async def __aexit__(self, *a): self.closed.set()

    async def send(self, payload: str):
        msg = json.loads(payload)
        self.sent.append(msg)
        if msg["type"] == "session.update":
            await self.incoming.put(json.dumps({"type": "session.updated"}))
        if msg["type"] == "input_audio_buffer.append" and sum(
            m["type"] == "input_audio_buffer.append" for m in self.sent) == 2:
            # server VAD detects end of speech and transcribes the turn
            await self.incoming.put(json.dumps({
                "type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed",
                "item_id": "item_1", "transcript": "hello there"}))
```

Output on `main`:

```text
EVENT_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT = 1000s
stream still open 5s after add_audio(None); events so far: ['turn_started', 'voice_stream_event_audio', 'turn_ended']
sent to server after end of input: ['session.update', 'input_audio_buffer.append', 'input_audio_buffer.append']
```

### Expected behavior

After `add_audio(None)`, pending speech is committed and transcribed, then the STT session closes, `session_ended` is emitted and `result.stream()` finishes.

A possible fix: on `None`, commit the buffer if speech was detected but not yet committed (committing an empty buffer returns a server error, which the listener currently treats as fatal), then close the websocket once the committed items have their transcripts or after a short grace period, so `_handle_events` receives `WebsocketDoneSentinel`. I'm happy to share a patch if it helps.

title: Streamed runs swallow consumer cancellation and skip run cleanup while a parallel input guardrail is running

judge.reasoning:
Both patches make the same core change: `_await_task_safely` and `input_guardrail_tripwire_triggered_for_stream` switch from `await task` to `asyncio.wait((task,))`, forward consumer cancellation to the task, and re-raise, so a cancelled guardrail task no longer looks like the waiter's own cancellation. Both pass the four independent tests for the issue's two repro scenarios (consumer timeout/cancel swallowed; result.cancel() during an in-flight tool skipping cleanup).

The decisive difference is the fifth independent test: `result.cancel()` called after the model finished, while the run loop's `finally` is already waiting on the guardrail. Here the CancelledError genuinely belongs to the run-loop task, so both patches' guardrail helper re-raises it. Patch A then lets it abort the rest of `start_streaming`'s `finally`, so computers are never disposed and the trace/spans never finish (independent test: FAIL-ASSERT on A, 'computer created for the run was not disposed'). Patch B explicitly catches that CancelledError in run_loop.py, finishes `dispose_resolved_computers()`, span/trace finish, and the completion sentinel, then re-raises it. The issue's stated expectation is general: 'cancelling the run should still finish the trace/spans and dispose per-run computers', and this is a very plausible ordering (fast model, slow moderation guardrail, user cancels). B resolves it; A does not. B also adds a regression test (`test_cancel_while_run_loop_awaits_input_guardrail_finishes_run_cleanup`) for exactly this path.

Patch A's additional work is mixed. The try/finally around model-provider/sandbox cleanup in `stream_events` is reasonable hardening now that cancellation propagates, but the base already skips those cleanups on the `cancelled` path, so B's behaviour is consistent with existing semantics rather than a regression. A's `ignore_cancelled` keyword on `input_guardrail_tripwire_triggered_for_stream` adds API surface and forces a signature change in an unrelated existing test's monkeypatched finalizer; B's unconditional `if not task.cancelled(): task.result()` is simpler and matches the issue's root-cause description. A's extra `await asyncio.wait((task,))` after `task.cancel()` preserves old direct-await settlement, which is defensible but not required by the issue.

Tests: both add deterministic, event-gated tests that would fail on base. B's are more directly mapped to the issue's scenarios (consumer cancel, consumer timeout, result.cancel during tool, consumer cancel during tool, cancel while run loop awaits guardrail, consumer cancel during run-loop cleanup wait). B's only skip is the `asyncio.timeout()` test on Python < 3.11, and it is paired with a non-skipped CancelledError equivalent, so coverage holds. A's parametrized consumer-cancellation test and cleanup-ordering test are solid but one of A's tests relies on fairly intricate monkeypatching of internals.

On correctness, B covers strictly more of the issue's stated expected behaviour, confirmed by the independent run, with a smaller and clearer change. B wins.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes, including the streaming cancellation section.
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #2222 fixed cancellation while `stream_events()` waits for the next event; this report covers the remaining waits on the input guardrail task and the run-loop task, which still swallow cancellation.

### Describe the bug

Streamed runs mishandle cancellation while a parallel input guardrail is still running. Parallel is the default for input guardrails, and a guardrail that outlasts the model, such as a moderation call, is common.

1. **The consumer's cancellation is swallowed.** When the model has finished but the guardrail has not, `stream_events()` waits for the guardrail after the final event. If the consumer is cancelled or its `asyncio.timeout()` expires during that wait, the guardrail is cancelled, but `stream_events()` returns normally. The caller never sees `CancelledError`/`TimeoutError` and continues with `result.final_output`, even though the input guardrail never produced a verdict.
2. **Run cleanup is skipped after `result.cancel()`.** If `result.cancel()` (or consumer cancellation) happens while the guardrail is running, the run loop's `finally` awaits the cancelled guardrail task, gets its `CancelledError`, and aborts the rest of cleanup. The trace plus the task and agent spans are never finished, and computers created by a `ComputerProvider` for the run are never disposed.

### Debug information
- Agents SDK version: v0.22.3 and `main` at 08e5c431
- Python version: 3.12.13 (the regression tests also run on 3.10)
- Operating system: macOS
- Model and model provider: none; reproduced with `agents.testing.ScriptedModel`
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

### Repro steps

```python
import asyncio

from agents import (
    Agent,
    GuardrailFunctionOutput,
    Runner,
    add_trace_processor,
    function_tool,
    input_guardrail,

from agents.testing import ScriptedModel, assistant_message, function_call

            pass

```

Output on `main`:

```text
1) timeout: stream_events() returned normally, final_output = 'done'
2) result.cancel(): unfinished traces = 1
```

### Expected behavior

```text
1) timeout: TimeoutError raised
2) result.cancel(): unfinished traces = 0
```

Cancelling a stream consumer should propagate to that consumer, and cancelling the run should still finish the trace/spans and dispose per-run computers.

### Root cause

Both waits await the shared task directly:

- `RunResultStreaming._await_task_safely()` runs `await task` and suppresses `CancelledError`. Awaiting a task forwards the waiter's cancellation into the task, so after the consumer is cancelled the task ends cancelled. The `CancelledError` the consumer then receives looks like the task's own cancellation and is swallowed.
- `input_guardrail_tripwire_triggered_for_stream()`, which the run loop's `finally` calls before disposing computers and finishing spans, runs `await task`. When the guardrail task was cancelled by `cancel()`, awaiting it raises `CancelledError` in the run loop and the remaining cleanup is skipped.

Ordering for (1): the model completes, `QueueCompleteSentinel` is queued, the consumer takes the sentinel and awaits the guardrail task, and the consumer is cancelled. The guardrail is cancelled, the consumer suppresses the resulting `CancelledError`, and `stream_events()` ends normally.

Ordering for (2): a tool (or the model) is in flight while the guardrail runs, and `result.cancel()` cancels the run loop and the guardrail. The run loop enters its `finally`, awaits the cancelled guardrail task, gets `CancelledError`, and exits before `dispose_resolved_computers()`, `span.finish()`, and `trace.finish()`.

Waiting with `asyncio.wait((task,))` avoids both problems: the task's own cancellation is not raised into the waiter, and a `CancelledError` there always belongs to the waiter. That waiter can then forward its cancellation to the task, as `await` did, and re-raise it.

title: gpt-4o-transcribe is being retired (config.py)

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the same core change, switching DEFAULT_STT_MODEL in src/agents/voice/models/openai_model_provider.py from gpt-4o-transcribe to gpt-transcribe, and all four independent tests go from FAIL-ASSERT on base to PASS on both, so correctness on the issue's ask is equal. The difference is in scope and risk. Patch A adds a focused test that asserts the default STT model name is gpt-transcribe and that an explicit model still overrides it; it would fail before and pass after, and nothing else changes. Patch B bundles two things the issue never asks for: (1) an unrelated pyproject.toml change to the sqlalchemy extra (SQLAlchemy[asyncio]), which is pure dependency churn in a model-rename fix, and (2) a behavioural change in openai_stt.py that, via a hard-coded string compare on self.model == 'gpt-transcribe', drops the language kwarg and re-sends it as extra_body={'languages': [...]}. Nothing in the issue supports that the replacement model rejects the language parameter, and the independent test with language set passes identically on A and B, so this remap earns no credit and adds risk: it is a brittle special case that would not apply to any other model name, and it is applied only to the non-streamed path while the streamed session code is untouched (yet B's streamed test asserts a 'languages' key, so that test's validity depends on unchanged code already behaving that way). B's wire-level tests are more thorough than A's, but thoroughness in tests does not offset unrelated dependency edits and speculative API-shape changes mixed into a one-line default swap. A resolves the issue at its root with no extraneous risk, so A is the better fix.

issue_md:
Hi, quick heads-up in case this isn't already on your radar.

OpenAI is shutting down `gpt-4o-transcribe` on February 26, 2027.

It looks like openai-agents-python still uses it, where it's DEFAULT_STT_MODEL. It's still there on the default branch as of October 1:

[`src/agents/realtime/config.py:86`](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/32edd3c3ecde37a7fb6bf4b082f35f1d8f7f086b/src/agents/realtime/config.py#L86)

OpenAI's replacement is `gpt-transcribe`.

There's still time, but the provider sets the date and it won't move.

How I found it: I maintain [DocsWatcher](https://github.com/jameskomo/docswatcher), an open source scanner that checks code against the deprecation notices providers publish. I ran it over the 50 most-starred repos tagged `openai`. Most of what it turns up is model names sitting in lists and price tables, which don't break anything, so I set those aside and read every hit in real code myself before opening anything. This one looked like a real call to me, but you know your code and I don't, so if I've got it wrong just say so and I'll close this.

Nothing to adopt here. I just thought you'd want to know.

title: After an approval, the resumed run records the approved tool span outside the agent span

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause the same way: they open the agent span before `resolve_interrupted_turn` on resume in both the blocking (`run.py`) and streamed (`run_loop.py`) paths, remove the later span-open block so it is not duplicated, and add `attach_generic_agent_error` to the streaming top-level exception handler so a resumed tool failure that bypasses the per-turn handler still marks the agent span with 'Error in agent run'. The independent tests confirm both resolve every scenario in the issue (parenting with task/turn spans on and off, streamed and not, stop_on_first_tool, and the error case). The differences are in completeness and testing. Patch A additionally threads the agent span into `resolve_interrupted_turn` and populates `span_data.tools`/`span_data.handoffs` from the resolved tools, so an agent span whose run ends on the approved tool (stop_on_first_tool or a raising tool) carries the same tool/handoff metadata it would have had without the interruption; Patch B leaves those lists empty in that case, a small but real inconsistency with the non-approval span the issue uses as its reference. Patch A's test is substantially more thorough: 16 parametrized cases covering continue, stop, error and handoff outcomes across streamed/non-streamed and task/turn spans on/off, and it asserts span parenting, tool/handoff metadata, both error messages, that every span ends, that span_start/span_end counts balance, and that no span is left current after the run — the last three guard against the main regression risk of opening the span earlier (a leaked or unbalanced span on a handoff or early return). Patch B's two tests cover success and error for both modes but do not cover stop_on_first_tool, handoff, or span-balance. Patch B's `start_agent_span` helper is a nice de-duplication and slightly cleaner craft, and its minimal placement right before `resolve_interrupted_turn` is tidy, but that does not outweigh A's broader verification and more complete agent span. A's extra parameter on `resolve_interrupted_turn` is a modest scope extension but directly serves the issue's expected behaviour and adds little risk.

### Please read this first

- Read the docs: yes.
- Searched for related issues: yes. #5045 dealt with trace reattachment on resume; nothing covers span parents.

### Describe the bug

After `state.approve(...)`, the resumed run executes the approved tool before it opens its agent span. The function span becomes a child of the task span, or of the trace root when task and turn spans are off. Only the paused span from the first run (`docs/tracing.md:147`) sits inside an agent span. If the approved tool has `failure_error_function=None`, as below, and raises, the resumed run ends without an agent span or `Error in agent run`.

`resolve_interrupted_turn` runs at `src/agents/run.py:1115` while `current_span` is still `None` (`:928`). The agent span opens later, at `:1492-1504`. The streamed path has the same order, at `src/agents/run_internal/run_loop.py:1323` and `:1564-1576`.

### Debug information

- Agents SDK version: 0.22.3 from PyPI, the `v0.23.0` tag, and `main` at `a575a6e`
- Related library versions: `openai` 3.23.0, `pydantic` 2.13.5 (PyPI install)
- Python version: 3.12.3 (PyPI install), 3.14.7 (`v0.23.0` and `main`)
- Operating system: Ubuntu 24.04
- Model and model provider: none, `agents.testing.ScriptedModel`
- Reproduces with the latest release: yes, PyPI 0.22.3 and the `v0.23.0` tag (not on PyPI yet).
- Consistent or intermittent: consistent, with `Runner.run` and `Runner.run_streamed`.

### Repro steps

```python
import asyncio
import sys

from agents import Agent, Runner, add_trace_processor, function_tool
from agents.testing import ScriptedModel, assistant_message, function_call
from agents.tracing import TracingProcessor

STREAMED = "--streamed" in sys.argv
spans = {}


class Spans(TracingProcessor):
    def on_trace_start(self, trace): pass
    def on_trace_end(self, trace): pass
    def on_span_start(self, span): pass
    def on_span_end(self, span): spans[span.span_id] = span
    def shutdown(self): pass
    def force_flush(self): pass


add_trace_processor(Spans())


def show(title):
    print(title)
    for s in sorted(spans.values(), key=lambda s: s.started_at):
        parent = spans.get(s.parent_id)
        where = f"{parent.span_data.type}" if parent else "trace root"
        error = f"  error={s.error['message']!r}" if s.error else ""
        print(f"    {s.span_data.type:8} {s.span_data.export().get('name', ''):8} parent={where}{error}")
    spans.clear()


@function_tool(name_override="refund", needs_approval=True, failure_error_function=None)
def approved_refund(order_id: str) -> str:
    return f"refunded {order_id}"


@function_tool(name_override="refund", needs_approval=True, failure_error_function=None)
def approved_failing_refund(order_id: str) -> str:
    raise RuntimeError("payments API down")


@function_tool(name_override="refund", failure_error_function=None)
def failing_refund(order_id: str) -> str:
    raise RuntimeError("payments API down")


async def run(agent, input):
    if STREAMED:
        result = Runner.run_streamed(agent, input)
        async for _ in result.stream_events():
            pass
        return result
    return await Runner.run(agent, input)


def agent_with(tool):
    model = ScriptedModel(
        [[function_call("refund", {"order_id": "A1"}, call_id="c1")], [assistant_message("done")]]
    )
    return Agent(name="support", model=model, tools=[tool])


async def main():
    try:
        await run(agent_with(failing_refund), "refund A1")
    except Exception as e:
        show(f"no approval, tool raises ({type(e).__name__}):")
    for tool in (approved_refund, approved_failing_refund):
        agent = agent_with(tool)
        first = await run(agent, "refund A1")
        spans.clear()  # the first run's paused refund span sits under its turn
        state = first.to_state()
        state.approve(first.interruptions[0])
        try:
            await run(agent, state)
            outcome = "completed"
        except Exception as e:
            outcome = type(e).__name__
        show(f"resumed after approval, tool {'raises' if tool is approved_failing_refund else 'succeeds'} ({outcome}):")


asyncio.run(main())
```

```text
no approval, tool raises (UserError):
    task     task     parent=trace root
    agent    support  parent=task  error='Error in agent run'
    turn     turn     parent=agent
    function refund   parent=turn  error='Error running tool'
resumed after approval, tool succeeds (completed):
    task     task     parent=trace root
    function refund   parent=task
    agent    support  parent=task
    turn     turn     parent=agent
resumed after approval, tool raises (UserError):
    task     task     parent=trace root
    function refund   parent=task  error='Error running tool'
# main a575a6e; --streamed, the v0.23.0 tag and PyPI 0.22.3 print the same; not run: the default OpenAI exporter
```

### Expected behavior

The approved tool span sits under the agent span, as it does without approval, and as `tests/test_agent_tracing.py:288-292` asserts for function spans. An approved tool whose exception ends the run leaves `Error in agent run` on that agent span.

@seratch, is opening the agent span before `resolve_interrupted_turn` on resume the fix you would take?

title: Run-wide tool exception formatting: add `tool_exception` kind to `RunConfig.tool_error_formatter`

judge.reasoning: Both patches add `kind="tool_exception"` with an `error` field, apply the run formatter only on the default failure path, preserve `failure_error_function=None` re-raising, fall back to the default on formatter crash or non-string return, and pass all independent tests. The differences are in coverage and completeness. Patch A triggers the formatter whenever the tool's failure handler *is* `default_tool_error_function`, so SDK-built tools that pass the default explicitly (`Agent.as_tool`, MCP tools) also get the run-wide policy; it adds tests for both and wires the formatter into realtime sessions with a test. That matches the issue's motivation ("one run-wide policy" so tools added later don't silently fall back) and the stated rule that it applies "when a tool uses the default failure_error_function". Patch B keys off the existing `_use_default_failure_error_function` flag only, deliberately excludes as_tool/MCP tools and `MCPToolCancellationError`, and documents these gaps in a docstring; that leaves the issue's run-wide goal unmet for a common class of tools and adds exclusions the issue never asked for. B also ships no documentation changes, whereas A updates `docs/running_agents.md` and `docs/tools.md` where the formatter kinds are enumerated, and updates the `default_tool_error_function` docstring. On craft, A factors the logic into a clearly named helper with `_debug.DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA`-aware logging; B inlines a nested block inside the existing function. B's test file is larger and includes useful redaction/namespace checks (and uses `qualified_tool_name`, a minor plus), but several tests exist to lock in B's own exclusions rather than the issue's behaviour, and the concurrency/cancellation test is tangential. Weighing correctness and scope against the issue's ask, A is the more complete and better-integrated fix.

### Please read this first

- [x] Have you read the docs? (Tools, RunConfig)
- [x] Have you searched for related issues? (closest: #2658 / #3707, which added `tool_error_formatter` for other kinds)

### Describe the feature

Since 0.23.0 (#5112), `default_tool_error_function` returns a fixed `"An error occurred while running the tool. Please try again."`. That is a sensible secure default. The only way to send approved error detail back to the model is a `failure_error_function` on **each** tool.

Apps with many tools usually want one run-wide policy instead. For example, "expose messages from our own `ToolInputError`, redact everything else". Today that means decorating every `@function_tool` call site. Tools added later silently fall back to the generic message, so the model can no longer self-correct bad arguments.

`RunConfig.tool_error_formatter` already exists for this kind of per-run policy, but `ToolErrorFormatterArgs.kind` only covers `"approval_rejected"` and `"tool_not_found"`.

**Proposal:** add a `kind="tool_exception"` to `tool_error_formatter`, with the exception on the args (e.g. `error: Exception | None`). It would apply only when a tool uses the default `failure_error_function`, and returning `None` keeps the redacted default. Precedence would be: an explicit per-tool `failure_error_function` wins, then the run-level formatter, then the SDK default. Secure by default is preserved, and nothing changes unless the formatter opts in.

```python
class ToolInputError(Exception): ...

def formatter(args: ToolErrorFormatterArgs) -> str | None:
    if args.kind == "tool_exception" and isinstance(args.error, ToolInputError):
        return f"Invalid input: {args.error}"
    return None  # keep SDK default

Runner.run(agent, input, run_config=RunConfig(tool_error_formatter=formatter))
```

### Repro of current behaviour (0.23.1 vs 0.22.3)

A tool that raises `ValueError("order_id must start with 'ORD-', got '123'")`, run with a fake model that captures the next turn's input:

| version | `function_call_output` sent to the model |
|---|---|
| 0.22.3 | `An error occurred while running the tool. Please try again. Error: order_id must start with 'ORD-', got '123'` |
| 0.23.1 | `An error occurred while running the tool. Please try again.` |

On 0.23.1 the only fix is per tool (`@function_tool(failure_error_function=...)`). There is no run-wide equivalent.

Happy to help test a change if useful.

+class ToolInputError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def _tool_outputs(model: ScriptedModel) -> list[Any]:
+    second_turn_input = model.calls[-1].input
+    assert isinstance(second_turn_input, list)
+    return [
+        item.get("output")
+        for item in second_turn_input
+        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "function_call_output"
+    ]
+
+
+async def _run_failing_tool(
+    *,
+    formatter: Any,
+    error: Exception,
+    streaming: bool = False,
+    **tool_kwargs: Any,
+) -> list[Any]:
+    def lookup_order(order_id: str) -> str:
+        raise error
+
+    tool = function_tool(lookup_order, **tool_kwargs)
+    model = ScriptedModel()
+    agent = Agent(name="test", model=model, tools=[tool])
+    model.extend(
+        [
+            [get_function_tool_call("lookup_order", '{"order_id": "123"}', call_id="call_1")],
+            [get_text_message("done")],

+    )
+    run_config = RunConfig(tool_error_formatter=formatter)
+    if streaming:
+        streamed = Runner.run_streamed(agent, input="start", run_config=run_config)

+            pass

+    def formatter(args: ToolErrorFormatterArgs[Any]) -> str | None:

title: RunState.add_input input is silently dropped under stop_at_tool_names

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the same core change: in RunState.add_input they widen the stop_at_tool_names check from the interrupted tools only to every function call in the last processed response (adding both name and qualified_name), which is exactly the root cause the issue identifies and matches the set resolve_interrupted_turn evaluates. The independent tests confirm both fix the reported scenario identically (base FAIL on the rejection and silent-drop tests, both patches PASS, control case passes everywhere). The meaningful difference is B's additional condition that skips the completed-sibling names when the interrupted response also contains a pending handoff. In the runner, handoffs are resolved before the tool_use_behavior final-output check, so a response with a handoff continues with the receiving agent and does call the model again; in that case A would wrongly refuse valid input (a false rejection against the contract the issue states: raise only when the model will not be called again), while B accepts it and its parametrized test asserts the input reaches the delegate's model call. B's test also covers the qualified-name case via tool_namespace, the unrelated-stop-name control, streamed and serialized variants, in one table. A's tests are also solid (4 parametrizations, a nested agent-as-tool stop case, and a control case) and A's code is simpler and conservative, but it over-rejects in the handoff case. Minor craft nit against B: the handoff carve-out applies only to the completed siblings, not to the pre-existing interrupted-tool-name set, which is slightly inconsistent, and both patches' test helpers (from_json/from_string, namespace kwarg, model.extend) could not be verified here. On balance B models the resume semantics more precisely without adding unrelated churn, so B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Please read this first

- **Have you read the docs?** Yes, the human-in-the-loop and agents pages.
- **Have you searched for related issues?** Yes. #5239 (fixed by #5240) is the resume behaviour this builds on; I found nothing about `add_input` in this state.

### Describe the bug

When one model response contains a tool listed in `stop_at_tool_names` that needs no approval and a sibling call that needs approval, the stop tool runs and the turn is interrupted. `RunState.add_input(...)` accepts new input on that state. After the approval, the resumed run ends on the stop tool's output without calling the model again (the behaviour #5240 introduced), so the staged input is never sent to the model and does not appear in `to_input_list()`. No error or warning is raised. With `tool_use_behavior="stop_on_first_tool"` the same `add_input` call is refused with `UserError: Cannot add input to an interrupted RunState whose tool result may end the run`.

On 0.22.3 the input did reach the model, because the resume ignored the completed stop tool (#5239). Since 0.23.0 the input is lost.

### Debug information
- Agents SDK version: 0.23.1 (also checked the code on `main` at 125efa02, unchanged)
- Related library versions (optional, e.g. `any-llm`, `litellm`, or `pydantic`): none needed
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating system: Linux (Pop!_OS 24.04)
- Model and model provider: none, `agents.testing.ScriptedModel`, no network
- Does the issue reproduce with the latest Agents SDK release? Yes, 0.23.1
- Does the issue occur consistently or intermittently? Consistently

Output of the script below on 0.23.1:

```text
python: 3.12.3
openai-agents: 0.23.1
  stop_on_first_tool                 add_input=rejected (UserError) final_output='finish:x' model_calls=1 input_sent_to_model=False input_in_history=False
  stop_at_tool_names=['finish']      add_input=accepted             final_output='finish:x' model_calls=1 input_sent_to_model=False input_in_history=False
expected: with stop_at_tool_names=['finish'] add_input is rejected the same way as under stop_on_first_tool, because the resumed run ends on the completed 'finish' result and never calls the model again
```

### Repro steps

```python
"""RunState.add_input accepts input that is then silently dropped when a completed
stop_at_tool_names sibling ends the resumed run."""

import asyncio
import importlib.metadata
import os
import platform

os.environ.setdefault("OPENAI_API_KEY", "sk-test")
os.environ.setdefault("OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING", "1")

from agents import Agent, Runner, function_tool
from agents.testing import ScriptedModel, assistant_message, function_call

print(f"python: {platform.python_version()}")
print(f"openai-agents: {importlib.metadata.version('openai-agents')}")


@function_tool
def finish(x: str) -> str:
    """Stop tool."""
    return f"finish:{x}"


@function_tool(needs_approval=True)
def protected(y: str) -> str:
    """Approval-gated tool."""
    return f"protected:{y}"


async def run_case(label: str, behavior) -> None:
    model = ScriptedModel(
        steps=[
            [
                function_call("finish", {"x": "x"}, call_id="f1"),
                function_call("protected", {"y": "y"}, call_id="p1"),
            ],
            [assistant_message("model-ran-again")],
        ]
    )
    agent = Agent(name="a", model=model, tools=[finish, protected], tool_use_behavior=behavior)
    first = await Runner.run(agent, "go")
    state = first.to_state()
    try:
        state.add_input("please also do Z")
        add_input = "accepted"
    except Exception as exc:
        add_input = f"rejected ({type(exc).__name__})"
    for item in first.interruptions:
        state.approve(item)
    resumed = await Runner.run(agent, state)
    seen_by_model = any("please also do Z" in str(call.input) for call in model.calls)
    in_history = "please also do Z" in str(resumed.to_input_list())
    print(
        f"  {label:34} add_input={add_input:20} final_output={resumed.final_output!r} "
        f"model_calls={len(model.calls)} "
        f"input_sent_to_model={seen_by_model} input_in_history={in_history}"
    )


async def main() -> None:
    await run_case("stop_on_first_tool", "stop_on_first_tool")
    await run_case(
        "stop_at_tool_names=['finish']", {"stop_at_tool_names": ["finish"]}
    )
    print(
        "expected: with stop_at_tool_names=['finish'] add_input is rejected the same way as "
        "under stop_on_first_tool, because the resumed run ends on the completed 'finish' "
        "result and never calls the model again"
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

With `stop_at_tool_names=["finish"]`, `add_input` should raise the same `UserError` it raises under `stop_on_first_tool`, because the resumed run is going to end on the completed `finish` result and never call the model again. Input that the state accepted should not disappear without an error.

**Cause.** `RunState.add_input` (`src/agents/run_state.py` 1072-1087 at 125efa02) decides whether the resume can end the run by intersecting `stop_at_tool_names` with the names of the interrupted tools only. Since #5240, `resolve_interrupted_turn` (`src/agents/run_internal/turn_resolution.py` 2869-2904) also feeds the outputs of siblings that already completed in the same response into the `tool_use_behavior` check, so a stop tool that already ran ends the run, and `add_input` does not account for that.

**Possible fix.** In `add_input`, compare `stop_at_tool_names` with every function call in the interrupted response (the completed siblings as well as the pending ones), the same set that `resolve_interrupted_turn` now evaluates, and add a test with a stop tool plus an approval-gated sibling that asserts `add_input` raises.
